Better not to speak. She had finally managed to get inside; she didn’t want to risk being chased out again.

Sitting at a slight distance from him, Shu You applied the medicine. When she grew bored, she picked up a pastry from the tray and began to nibble on it. A light, sandalwood fragrance wafted over, and after a while, she felt so comfortable that she grew drowsy.

It felt so good. Shu You’s head drooped lower and lower, as if she might fall asleep at any moment.

Just as her entire body was about to slump to the ground, she jolted awake, staring blankly at the man’s back. She had actually almost fallen asleep while sitting with him.

Even though she had barely slept the night before due to the unfamiliar bed, and her temples had ached slightly that morning, now all discomfort had vanished without a trace.

The storybook... no, the divine book hadn’t lied to her after all.

His very presence was so restorative, what else about him would be...

Shu You didn’t dare think further. A blush crept up her cheeks, and she stuffed several large mouthfuls of pastry into her mouth to distract herself from her wandering thoughts.

As she shook her head to dispel the images in her mind, she didn’t notice that Song Ling had already stood up, his gaze lingering on her.

"What’s wrong?" Shu You sensed the gaze and looked up, unaware that a few crumbs were clinging to the corner of her mouth. Seeing him staring at her without a word, she unconsciously licked her lips.

Puzzled, she touched her cheek, and her fingertip came away sticky.

Realizing what it was, Shu You’s fair face flushed crimson in an instant. She looked at the now-empty white jade plate, the entire box of pastries had been devoured by her. A wave of embarrassment washed over her.

Xiao Ling turned his head to glance at the sky outside. Was it that hot today?

The girl’s face and neck were flushed red, as if she were a ripe tomato, radiating heat.

Why was her face so red?

"Young Master Song, I’ll make you more next time," she said, too embarrassed for words. She had brought him pastries, only to eat them all herself. She had no idea how her appetite had suddenly become so ravenous.

"No need. I’ve told you before, I don’t like sweets." With that, he took a step forward and left.

Shu You quickly stood up, grabbing the tray and hurriedly following after him.

She followed him all the way until he suddenly stopped in front of a rockery. She accidentally bumped into him and then hastily stepped back.

"How long do you plan to follow me?" Xiao Ling had led this little shadow quite a distance, and seeing that she had no intention of leaving, he finally stopped and urged her to go.

Don’t keep following him.

Shu You’s throat tightened slightly. She had originally thought to wait for him to stop so she could say goodbye, but he had walked so quickly that she thought he was taking her somewhere.

"You didn’t say... I thought..."

Oh well, he clearly didn’t like her, so why would he want to spend so much time with her? She thought to herself, but still couldn’t help but purse her lips.

Anyway, she had absorbed enough today. She might as well leave.

"That... I’ll..." Before Shu You could finish her sentence, she suddenly heard footsteps coming from behind the rockery. She didn’t know why she panicked, as if her relationship with Song Ling was something that couldn’t be seen in the light. In her haste, she grabbed the man’s sleeve and pulled him into hiding behind the rockery.

Xiao Ling didn’t react in time and was tugged along, squeezing into the narrow space behind the rockery with her.

Just as he was about to speak, a finger pressed against his lips. The girl in front of him shook her head, signaling him to be quiet. There were only a few inches between them, and from a distance, it looked as if they were embracing.

Shu You’s heart was in chaos. She tilted her ear, listening carefully as the footsteps faded away, unaware that her finger had slightly pressed into the man’s lips, the knuckles fitting snugly against the gap.

After the group of people had left, Shu You let out a sigh of relief. Only then did she realize how close she was to him, almost pressed against him. His refined face was right in front of her; if she stood on her tiptoes, she could kiss him. She instinctively took a few steps back. "I’m sorry, I was presumptuous again."

But in her heart, she secretly rejoiced. She had gained another advantage, this should last her three days, right?

Following Song Ling out from behind the rockery, Shu You abandoned her persistent thoughts and softly bid farewell. "Young Master Song, it’s getting late. I won’t disturb you any longer."

The tall figure ahead seemed to have heard her but chose not to respond. Shu You didn’t mind. She was in a good mood, and her steps unconsciously quickened. Unfortunately, her foot landed on a slippery patch of moss, and her body lurched forward, off-balance.

At that very moment, the man in front of her happened to be turning aside. *Thud.* His back slammed hard against the rockery.

Shu You tensed up, closing her eyes. This was it, she was going to fall painfully. Her hands flailed, and she grabbed onto something. A muffled groan reached her ears. She opened her eyes and saw that it was Song Ling’s belt.

Her chin was pressed against his lower abdomen. Shu You looked up and saw that Song Ling’s back was pressed against the rockery, his cold, handsome face contorted with a hint of pain. His beautifully shaped thin lips let out a few ragged breaths.

It actually sounded... kind of nice.

After a few seconds of stunned silence, the two of them made belated eye contact. Shu You’s hand tightly clutched the belt, and as she stared at the prominent, taut muscles beneath his fair skin, she couldn’t help but swallow. She hadn’t meant to.

The curve of her chin was unmistakable, and the place where they touched instantly burned.

Shu You’s mind was a muddled mess, and a strange thought suddenly surfaced: *He’s quite well-endowed, just like in the stories.*

She wondered how long this would buy her...

---

chapters.title: Do You Like Me, Young Master?
chapters.content:
The young man was still sitting on the ground, his cold, sharp eyes unusually distracted, as if he hadn’t fully processed what had happened.

This place seemed so vulnerable, had she damaged something?

The muscles beneath her fingers on his abdomen were trembling slightly.

In the next moment, a sudden flick against her cheek startled her. Shu You’s heart jolted, and she quickly stood up, moving away. Her entire face burned, radiating heat.

Seemed like nothing was broken.

She stood there, stammering, unsure of how to speak. She tentatively stretched out her hand toward him, her voice trembling. "I-I’m sorry, Young Master Song. I just tripped a moment ago. It wasn’t intentional. Let me help you up?"

Not only had she fallen, but she had also touched *there*, even more intimate than their first encounter.

The man seemed to come to his senses. He lowered his gaze, ignoring the outstretched hand, and used the rockery to push himself up, saying nothing.

This was bad, he was definitely angry. Shu You didn’t dare to follow. She stayed in place, watching him leave.

A gust of wind blew, and Shu You sneezed. Looking down at her mud-stained skirt, she didn’t hesitate before turning and heading back to her room.

"Miss, where have you been?" Huanxi was in the middle of sewing when she saw her mistress enter, covered in dirt. She immediately stood up to greet her.

Shu You let out a soft sigh and waved her hand before removing her clothes one by one, allowing Huanxi to clean her with a warm, damp towel.

"I just fell. I’m just a little dirty. It doesn’t hurt."

Because she had fallen onto Song Ling... and touched...

A thought suddenly struck Shu You, and she let out a light cough, her entire body feeling uncomfortable.

"Miss, is your throat bothering you?" Huanxi handed her a cup of hot tea, her brows furrowed with concern. "Drink some tea to soothe it."

"I’m fine. I’ll be better after resting a bit." Shu You snapped back to reality. Her fair face, devoid of makeup, was flushed from the wiping.

After returning to her room, she felt uncomfortable all over. Only after removing all her hairpins and ornaments did she feel better. Lost in thought, she absentmindedly rubbed her cheek too hard and winced when the pain registered.

Huanxi turned and picked up a jar of face cream, gently applying it to Shu You’s face with meticulous care, as if handling a precious treasure.

"Miss, it’s almost time for lunch. Will you be going to the vegetarian hall to eat today? Or should I bring the meal here for you?"

Huanxi’s voice was as soft as if she were coaxing a child. Seeing her mistress’s dazed expression and her reluctance to speak, she knew Shu You didn’t want to talk about it. She also didn’t press for answers, wanting her to rest in the room to avoid unnecessary movement.

"Okay, okay." Shu You quickly agreed. Although she had eaten a whole plate of pastries and wasn’t hungry, going to the vegetarian hall might mean running into Song Ling. After the earlier embarrassment, it was better to avoid him for now.

Huanxi nodded and left the room.

...

The night was deep, and dew was heavy. The rear wing of Changshan Temple was silent, save for the rustling of leaves in the gentle wind.

Inside the room, the candlelight had burned out, gradually swallowed by the darkness. Behind the thin curtains, a figure could be faintly seen. A young man, dressed in white sleeping robes, lay properly on the bed, his eyelids tightly shut in sleep.

But the young man’s chest beneath the covers was trembling slightly, his breathing rising and falling with each inhale and exhale. Sweat beaded on his forehead, his brows were tightly knit, and an unnatural flush colored his cheeks, as if he were trapped in a nightmare he couldn’t wake from.

"Young Master," the girl in his dream was even bolder than she was during the day. Dressed in thin silk, she sat on his lap, her tender arms hooked around his neck, her entire body pressed against his chest, her cheek tightly against the skin at his collar. "Young Master, why won’t you look at me?"

A faint, almost imperceptible fragrance wafted from her ear into his nose, followed by the warm breath from her lips as she spoke, spraying bit by bit onto his jaw and the back of his ear.

"Do you know what you’re doing?" Xiao Ling tried to push away the person in front of him, but the girl only tightened her arms around his neck, pulling him closer. Her soft body clung to him as if boneless.

"Of course I do, Shu You."

A chuckle sounded in his ear, and a hand caressed his cheek. Xiao Ling turned his face away to avoid it. "Don’t touch me."

The girl’s expression faltered. She pouted, burying her face in the side of his neck and softly whined, "Young Master, you’re so heartless. Why won’t you let me touch such a handsome face?"

"Your most important part already greeted me today. I was very happy about it."

Xiao Ling recalled how his ears had gradually turned red that day, how the girl had been lying on his abdomen, her limpid, affectionate eyes filled with innocence.

He should have pushed her away immediately, but the tingling sensation that spread through his body had left him stunned for a long time. By the time he returned to his room, half of his body was still numb.

It was an experience he had never had before, novel, strange, making him want to distance himself from it.

"Young Master, why aren’t you speaking?" The girl’s warm palm cupped his cheek, and she tilted her head slightly, pressing her lips to the corner of his mouth, leaving behind a damp sensation.

Xiao Ling suddenly came to his senses, his expression filled with disbelief and shyness. Before he could dodge, she cupped his face and kissed him.

"You like me too, don’t you?"

"I like you so much. It was love at first sight. Don’t push me away."

The shy yet direct confession caught Xiao Ling off guard. His lips parted slightly, and the girl’s lips, sweet as the finest pastry, tangled with his.

"Tell me you like me, okay?" Between breaths, he heard her soft plea. Xiao Ling lowered his lashes but gave no answer.

...

The sky was just beginning to lighten in the early morning, and faint light slowly seeped through the cracks in the door, entering the room. Xiao Ling suddenly opened his eyes, jolting awake from his dream. His face was flushed, and his chest heaved with rapid breaths.

He pressed a hand to his forehead, taking deep breaths. Everything that had happened in the dream was deeply etched into his mind, impossible to forget.

The lingering scent of the girl on his lips was sweet yet not cloying, making him want to immerse himself in it.

Xiao Ling abruptly threw off the covers and got up, walking to the round table where he gulped down the already cold tea. But the heat in his body didn’t subside in the slightest. He stared at the lonely sunlight, lost in thought.

Soon after, Xing Jue entered the courtyard carrying breakfast. Passing through the corridor, he noticed a patch of water on the ground that hadn’t dried yet and felt a flicker of curiosity. It hadn’t rained today.

Entering the room, he saw His Highness sitting at the desk, copying Buddhist scriptures. He softly called out, "Your Highness, it’s time for breakfast."

Xiao Ling merely hummed in response but didn’t get up. Xing Jue didn’t urge him further, instead standing respectfully to the side, waiting for orders.

His gaze inadvertently landed on the dampness at His Highness’s temples, not yet dry. He thought of the puddle in the courtyard. Could it be that the weather was too hot, and His Highness had taken a cold bath early in the morning?

But it was only May; it wasn’t even the hottest time of the year yet.

Still, he didn’t dare to speculate too much about His Highness’s thoughts. The fleeting idea passed through his mind and was immediately forgotten.

His Highness had his reasons, and as a subordinate, there was no need to pry. Taking care of his master was enough.

After what felt like a long time, Xing Jue finally saw him set down the brush. He stared at the paper, lost in thought, before speaking with an unchanging expression.

"Return to the palace."

"Yes, Your Highness." Xing Jue raised an eyebrow behind his back. Normally, when there was no morning court or urgent matters, His Highness would choose to stay at Changshan Temple. Yet now, he wanted to return to the palace.

The tall figure in front of him suddenly stopped and turned his head to give another order. "Investigate someone’s identity. As soon as possible."

Xing Jue was confused but still nodded in agreement.

chapters.title: If He Ignores Me, Then So Be It
chapters.content:
Shu You stayed in her room for two days without stepping outside. Each day, Xuanxi would bring meals from the vegetarian hall, and she would eat, sleep, and repeat. The stuffiness in her chest and the pain in her body vanished completely.

The illustrated books she had brought from the Marquis’s mansion were so engrossing that Shu You often covered her mouth to stifle laughter, her almond-shaped eyes, narrowed into crescents, constantly brimming with amusement.

"Xuanxi, I’ve finished this one. Your turn," she said. Whenever Shu You adored a book, she would recommend it to Xuanxi. The two of them would then delve into deep discussions afterward. Their tastes were remarkably similar, like two peas in a pod.

Shu You leaned against the windowsill, letting the warm breeze tousle the strands of hair by her temples. With one hand holding a book, she read with rapt attention, feeling utterly free and at ease.

Ever since she was little, she would cough at the slightest breeze, and she never went without a wind-blocking cloak. Rarely had she ever basked in the wind and sunlight like this. Even if it was only for a few days, she was thoroughly content.

"Miss!" Xuanxi returned to the room after washing and drying clothes in the small courtyard. Seeing Shu You sitting by the window in the breeze, she cried out in alarm and quickly stepped forward to close the window. "What if you catch a cold?"

Now that they were in the temple, unlike the Marquis’s mansion, there was no physician on standby. Falling ill would be troublesome.

But Shu You just laughed, grabbing Xuanxi’s wrist and pinching her cheek. Her pupils, filled with mirth, shone brightly, glistening like water. "Good Xuanxi, I’m feeling much better. I’ve been sitting here for so long and haven’t coughed once."

Her face, after being in the wind for so long, remained rosy and radiant. Her eyes were bright and full of vitality, her energy abundant, nothing like the frail, sickly appearance one would expect from someone with a long-term illness.

Xuanxi blinked in surprise, then her eyebrows and eyes lit up with joy, her voice brimming with delight. "This Changshan Temple really works! When Miss said Changshan Temple could make my body healthier, I didn’t believe it. But now I do. That’s wonderful."

Shu You grinned but didn’t immediately agree. Feigning an air of mystery, she said, "Now you see how amazing your miss is, don’t you? When have I ever lied to you?"

"Let me calculate where your future husband is right now," Shu You said, tapping her index and middle fingers against her thumb repeatedly. She closed her eyes and murmured softly, "Hmm… surprisingly, he’s…"

Before she could finish, Xuanxi, her face flushed with embarrassment, covered Shu You’s mouth with her hand, reducing her to muffled sounds.

"Miss mustn’t tease me anymore," Xuanxi said after letting go, her voice barely above a whisper. Her ears and the back of her neck were completely red. "I only want to serve Miss. I’ve never thought about getting married."

"Never thought about getting married, huh?" Shu You’s eyes flickered with mischief. She didn’t stop teasing. "But I heard that Mama Qin’s son…"

Seeing Xuanxi’s head nearly bow to the ground in shame, Shu You laughed and stopped. "Alright, I won’t tease you anymore."

Anyway, whether this works out or not, she would always make sure Xuanxi was well taken care of. Even if Xuanxi left, there was still her mother. She wouldn’t let anyone bully her.

Shu You turned her gaze back to the window, which faced the direction of Qiyun Hall. She wondered if Song Ling was still there.

Having avoided him for two days, Shu You sighed softly. She would go find him again tomorrow.

The next morning, after Xuanxi helped her dress and style her hair, Shu You took the Heart Sutra and stationed herself at the temple gates, waiting. Familiar with the place, she wiped the steps with her handkerchief and sat down, silently waiting.

She would just wait here. She didn’t believe he wouldn’t come.

Although she and Song Ling had only met a few times, and he was always cold toward her, their two physical contacts had been accidental.

But he had given her ointment after seeing her hands scalded, which showed he had some kindness in him. He wasn’t completely indifferent.

In both her past life and this one, Shu You had never met a man who was so cold toward her.

The feeling was novel and frustrating.

Forget it. She’d give him more patience. Maybe after some time, she could truly win him over. Besides, she didn’t want anything serious with him. A brief, casual romance wouldn’t hurt him.

After a quarter of an hour, Shu You heard footsteps and stood up abruptly, positioning herself at the temple gates with a smile. Her clear, watery autumn-like eyes looked toward the newcomer, and she called out sweetly, "Young Master Song."

But Song Ling acted as if he hadn’t seen her. Ignoring her completely, he walked past and entered the temple, the door closing in her face.

Shu You’s face was filled with shock. How could he be so rude? He clearly saw her but didn’t even acknowledge her, as if she didn’t exist.

It was just a touch! It wasn’t intentional!

Why was he so petty!

Furious, Shu You’s eyes widened, her beautiful brows and eyes tinged with anger. She wanted to take back her earlier assessment of him. This man was as stubborn as a wooden block. No one had ever treated her like this.

After a moment, she reasoned with herself.

It was she who needed something from him. Maybe he was so annoyed with her that he couldn’t be bothered to acknowledge her.

But as she thought this, a sense of grievance began to swell in her heart, and her eyes filled with hot tears, on the verge of falling.

If he ignored her, then so be it. Who cared?

Tears slid down Shu You’s beautiful face. After wiping them with her sleeve, she turned and left. She wanted to go home. Right now. In her past life, her body had been weak anyway. It was just another life. She accepted her fate.

After her graceful figure disappeared through the corridor, a few moments later, the temple door creaked open again. A refined figure stood silently at the doorway for a while before turning and going back inside. The door was never opened again.

As dusk fell, the setting sun bathed the sky in shades of orange, turning half the sky red.

Xiao Ling finished reciting the scriptures and walked slowly back to the small courtyard. As he passed through the corridor, a round head suddenly popped out from behind a red pillar, following him stealthily.

Wherever he went, she followed.

Shu You trailed behind him, constantly using objects to conceal herself. Having been at Changshan Temple for several days, she still didn’t know where he lived. This time, she was determined to find out!

As for the bold declaration she had made earlier, she had already forgotten most of it. Who would be so hard on themselves? Two months of hard work for a lifetime of happiness was a good deal.

For the sake of the future, what was a little grievance? Shu You saw the bigger picture. After walking a stretch, she wiped away her tears and turned back.

Giving up halfway was not an option. She had to see things through to the end. That was the lesson her father had taught her.

Besides, maybe Song Ling was just too shy to acknowledge her. Humph, what a little thing!

Trying to avoid being seen by Song Ling while also hiding from the passing monks was exhausting. Shu You crouched behind a stone railing to catch her breath, but when she stood up, she realized she had lost him.

Song Ling had disappeared.

She looked around but couldn’t find him.

Shu You lightly stamped her foot. It seemed today’s efforts were in vain again.

Suddenly, a familiar cold voice came from behind her.

"Are you looking for me?"

Shu You’s spine stiffened. Damn, she had been caught.

In her panic, a bold idea flashed through her mind. In the span of a few seconds, tears welled up in her eyes. She suddenly turned around and accurately threw herself into the arms of the man behind her. She wrapped her arms tightly around his waist, burying her face in his firm chest, her shoulders shaking as she sobbed.

"Where did you go? I was so scared alone."

"Don’t leave me behind, wuu."

So immersed was she in her act that she didn’t notice the man’s body had suddenly gone rigid. Mischievously, she rubbed her tears all over him, soaking a small patch of his clothes.

Hmph, she wanted to disgust him. How dare he ignore her earlier!

---

chapters.title: Why Is She So Clingy?
chapters.content:
Xiao Ling stood stunned for a moment. The soft, fragrant girl had thrown herself into his arms, her waist tightly encircled by two arms, his nose filled with her scent.

Her tearful, gentle voice entered his ears, coquettish and weak, as if she desperately needed him at that moment.

This feeling was extremely unfamiliar. She was like a beautiful little cat, exclusively his, baring her soft, snowy belly to lure him into petting her. Even without touching, he could sense the softness and tenderness there.

How did she end up hugging him like this?

This was improper!

Xiao Ling came back to his senses, his mind and body extremely uncomfortable. He twisted his body, trying to pry her arms away to distance himself. But the girl in his arms, as if sensing his intention, suddenly held on even tighter.

"Don’t push me away."

Hearing this, he felt a bit disoriented. Reality and dreams overlapped at this moment. In his dreams, she had said the exact same words, entwining around his neck and...

The soft skin, the tender lips, it all seemed real. Xiao Ling’s ears suddenly turned red. He averted his gaze, not daring to look anymore, and the force with which he pushed her away lessened considerably.

Why was this woman so clingy? She was simply...

Xiao Ling had been well-read since childhood, but at this moment, he couldn’t find the right words to describe her. A few days ago, he had sent Xingjuan to investigate her background and learned that she was an orphan with both parents deceased.

She didn’t know his true identity. If she wanted to attach herself to him, it was only to find someone she could entrust herself to. That was why she had sought him out.

Xiao Ling’s thoughts were exceptionally clear at this moment. Shu You must have taken a liking to him, falling for him at first sight, her feelings so intense she couldn’t extricate herself.

Huh? Why wasn’t she reacting when he pushed her?

Shu You had tightly held onto him, prepared to be pushed away. When she felt him trying to pry her arms apart, she swiftly wrapped her arms even tighter around him. Pressing her face against his chest, she boldly said, "Don’t push me away."

After saying this, he indeed stopped pushing her away. This man was unusually agreeable today, Shu You thought to herself.

She secretly rejoiced. Hugging him for a while would surely make her feel better for days. Who cared? As long as he didn’t push her away, she could take advantage of the situation a little longer.

Before long, a familiar cold voice came from above her head.

"How much longer are you going to hug me?"

Shu You immediately let go, looking up at the man. She noticed that although his expression was cold, the roots of his ears were bright red, standing out against his fair, jade-like skin.

So he was embarrassed.

"Young Master Song, I’m sorry. I got your clothes dirty," Shu You said, looking at the damp patch on his chest and secretly smiling as she bit her lip. He was so particular about cleanliness. It was good to annoy him for a bit.

Xiao Ling followed her gaze to his chest. The dampness had seeped into the fabric, sticking uncomfortably to his skin. Looking at her red, pitiful eyes, the words he had intended to say died on his lips.

All that came out was a dry, stiff sentence: "Men and women should not touch each other."

Forget it. This time, he would let it slide. Next time she came close, he would dodge faster and keep his distance.

Today, he had been caught off guard, allowing her to hold him so tightly. Xiao Ling would learn from this experience and not let it happen again.

Shu You knew when to stop. She nodded along with his words. It was true that men and women should not touch, but if she didn’t get close, how would she survive? He was now her "great treasure."

A treasure that could save her life.

Seeing him turn to leave and shake her off, Shu You pouted. "Young Master Song, I’m hungry."

The two of them locked eyes. Xiao Ling’s gaze was cold, his expression clear: if she was hungry, she should go find food. What did it have to do with him?

"But the vegetarian hall closed a long time ago. I waited for a long time at Qiyun Hall. It was so cold and I’m so hungry," Shu You said. Right on cue, her stomach growled. The monks ate only before noon, and since she didn’t know when he would come out, she had waited outside the entire time, having only eaten breakfast that day.

The girl before him lowered her gaze, her thick, curly lashes trembling slightly. She covered her stomach with both hands, looking pitiful.

A flicker of helplessness passed through Xiao Ling’s eyes. After taking a few steps, he saw her still standing in place, staring blankly at him. He frowned and said, "Follow me."

Silly girl. No wonder she had let herself go hungry.

Shu You responded with an "Oh," then lowered her head, bit her lip, and secretly smiled as she quickly followed behind.

Along the way, the two of them passed through several main halls, turning this way and that, the surroundings growing quieter. Changshan Temple was vast, and this was an area Shu You had never visited before.

As they walked, Shu You asked questions but only received a few "mm" responses from the man. She glanced at him secretly. It was as if speaking a few more words would cost him his life.

They arrived at a courtyard. Xiao Ling lightly pushed open the gate and walked in. Shu You hurried after him.

As soon as she entered, she saw a flower bed planted in the open space of the courtyard. The tender green leaves and colorful blossoms interwove, creating a beautiful sight, though she couldn’t identify the species.

This courtyard was huge, much larger than the one where she and Xuanxi stayed. She sneaked a few glances around and followed Xiao Ling into a side room.

"Wait here," he said with a glance. Shu You sat down at the round table, her eyes sparkling as she looked at him. She wanted to ask what there was to eat but stopped herself, afraid of being too presumptuous.

"You live here?" Shu You asked, looking through the open door at the courtyard. She was already eighty percent sure. No wonder she couldn’t find where he lived, it was so remote that finding it would be a miracle.

Fortunately, she was clever.

Xiao Ling gave a soft "mm" and sat down across from her, three seats away.

Sitting so far away, was he afraid she would pounce on him again? Shu You recalled how red his earlobes had been earlier and secretly smiled to herself.

Outside the room, faint footsteps could be heard, so soft that under normal circumstances, Shu You wouldn’t have noticed them. But the atmosphere between the two of them was so quiet that even the slightest sound stood out.

A young boy in blue, with clear brows and bright eyes, stepped over the threshold into the room. He looked up and met Shu You’s gaze, then smiled and nodded slightly.

This must be Xiao Ling’s servant. She should make a good impression to make things easier.

Xingjuan saw the Jiang girl from last time sitting across from his master. He lowered his head, and a flicker of shock passed through his eyes. In just a few days, his master had already brought her into his courtyard.

What had happened when he wasn’t by his master’s side? His curiosity grew.

"Master, would you like dinner?" Xingjuan quickly regained his composure and changed his form of address, lowering his head as he waited for instructions.

"Bring dinner."

Xingjuan received his order and quickly left the room. Before he disappeared, he stole a glance at Shu You. Their master actually liked this type?

She was delicate and lovely, as if she could be pinched to produce water.

No wonder he had ignored all the noble ladies who had tried to get close to him in the past.

Not daring to look any longer, Xingjuan walked toward the small kitchen.

After making several trips, the round table was filled with dishes. Though there was no meat, each dish was exquisite. Shu You was somewhat shocked. She hadn’t eaten this well since coming to the temple.

To avoid revealing her identity, she and Xuanxi usually ate whatever was available at the vegetarian hall. If they were really craving something, they would ask the monks who went down the mountain daily to bring back some pastries.

She hadn’t expected this guy to have his own private kitchen. She was jealous, so jealous.

Shu You followed his lead and picked up her chopsticks. When the crisp lotus root entered her mouth, she almost teared up. It was delicious.

She was so focused on the food that she didn’t notice a gaze silently watching her from the side.

Xingjuan stood to the side, stealing glances at the girl eating. She was beautiful and eye-catching. No wonder his master liked her.

Though she was a bit thin and frail, she needed to be well taken care of.

Those idiots at the Astronomical Bureau hadn’t mentioned anything about the Red Bird Star (a sign of marriage) when they calculated his master’s fortune this year. He had been caught completely off guard today.

Lost in thought, Xingjuan suddenly felt a gaze leisurely fall on him.

He met his master’s eyes and abruptly came to his senses, turning his head to look out the open door, not daring to look at Shu You, who was eating, any longer.

What kind of man would allow others to stare at the woman he loved? He had been careless.

After Xingjuan finished clearing the dishes, he quietly excused himself, leaving the two of them alone. He was afraid that if he stayed any longer, his master would not be able to resist demoting him back to the shadow guards.

chapters.title: Of Course She is Beautiful as a Flower, Stunningly Gorgeous
chapters.content:
The evening sky was vast and damp, the quiet darkness gradually swallowing all the light.

Under the table, Shu You's hands fidgeted restlessly, her heart wavering. If she asked him to take her back, would he agree?

The thought arose and then quickly retreated. He was so cold, he would definitely refuse.

Perhaps bringing her here for dinner had already exhausted his patience, and after the meal, he couldn’t wait for her to disappear.

But it was so dark outside...

The man across from her stood up, and Shu You quickly followed suit. Seeing him walk out without changing his expression, she reached out and tugged at his sleeve, her voice soft: "Song Ling..."

"What else is it?" Xiao Ling looked down at the delicate fingers by his sleeve, frowning slightly. Why were there so many things? After eating, what more did she want?

"Nothing," Shu You withdrew her hand. As expected, he was unwilling. "Then I'll go back first. Thank you, Young Master Song, for the dinner."

She thanked him softly and walked out of the courtyard along the path she had come, thinking that it was dark but not too late, so it shouldn’t be dangerous.

As Shu You stepped out of the courtyard gate, she was called to a stop. Xing Jue approached with a lit lantern, extending the other end of the wooden pole toward her.

"Miss Jiang, please. The lantern will light your way better."

A flicker of delight flashed in her eyes, and under the candlelight, her pupils seemed like liquid jade in a glass jar, shimmering brilliantly. "Thank you."

With the lantern, she was no longer afraid. Shu You nodded to him in gratitude before turning and walking away slowly.

The figure of the girl carrying the lantern grew farther and farther in the corridor, disappearing completely after turning the corner. Xing Jue was about to close the courtyard gate when he heard his lord, who had somehow appeared, slightly lift his chin to signal him to follow.

"Follow behind her and take her back. Don’t let her notice."

Xing Jue accepted the order, the corners of his lips curling slightly. "Yes."

His lord clearly liked her a lot, but he rarely interacted with the girl. He should have taken her back himself, and they could have talked along the way.

He was too clueless about romance. This way, he wouldn’t win the girl’s heart. Xing Jue shook his head secretly.

...

Shu You was extremely grateful that she wasn’t directionally challenged. Otherwise, with how far Song Ling’s courtyard was from her residence, she would have been lost long ago.

Seeing the light in her own room from afar, she quickened her pace. Huanxi must be waiting anxiously inside.

She blew out the lantern’s flame and pushed open the courtyard gate. Unaware of the figure that swiftly flashed behind her, she only heard the rustling of tree branches. When she turned to look, there was nothing.

Maybe it was a bird. She didn’t take it to heart.

"Miss, where did you go today?"

"You were gone for so long, I was worried to death."

As soon as she entered the house, Huanxi grabbed her and bombarded her with questions. Shu You patted her hand gently to soothe her, her soft voice calming the anxious heart. "I’m fine. I’m doing great. I just ran into some things today and was delayed. It won’t happen again."

With a few words, she managed to reassure Huanxi completely.

"Today, I was almost scared to death. Fortunately, Miss is fine," Huanxi said, after heating the water and finding a small stool to sit behind the bathtub, carefully helping Shu You untangle and comb her long, knotted hair. Her small face was full of seriousness and determination.

Shu You laughed, turning her head to glance at her. "Silly girl."

She thought about how, when she had hugged him earlier, Song Ling hadn’t pushed her away immediately. She was puzzled and, while drying herself with a towel, asked Huanxi.

"Huanxi, if there’s a man who is cold and indifferent, usually doesn’t like to talk to people, but after a few encounters with a woman, when that woman suddenly hugs him, and he doesn’t push her away, why would that be?"

Huanxi pondered for a moment before asking, "What does that woman look like? What’s her personality like?"

"Of course, she’s beautiful as a flower, stunningly gorgeous, and her personality is especially charming, unforgettable at first sight."

Huanxi didn’t stop her movements, her tone certain. "Then that man must have fallen for that woman, which is why he didn’t push her away. Who knows how happy he must be inside."

Shu You turned around in the bathtub, causing a splash of water. Her eyes flickered with doubt. "Really?"

"Of course it’s true," Huanxi said, the more she thought about it, the more she believed her guess was correct. But seeing her miss’s expression, which was somewhat suspicious, she asked, "Miss, that woman isn’t...?"

"Not at all, it’s not me," Shu You said with a composed face, but she turned back and bit her lower lip, her heart pounding with guilt. "You know your miss is brainstorming a new book. This is just a plot I’m thinking of."

Her excuse was reasonable, and Huanxi didn’t dwell on it, simply nodding without further questions.

But Huanxi’s answer didn’t quite align with what Shu You had in mind. With her beauty, few men would reject her. It must be that Song Ling, seeing her take the initiative, didn’t push her away.

It definitely wasn’t as Huanxi had said, that Song Ling had feelings for her.

If he truly liked her, why didn’t he take the initiative to send her back when it was so dark tonight? He didn’t even ask, and it was that little servant boy who thoughtfully gave her a lantern, which was why she wasn’t so scared.

That must be it!

She had been so proactive, and Song Ling still acted indifferent. The idea that he liked her was absurd.

Perhaps he couldn’t wait to never see her again.

Shu You lowered her head in deep thought as she stepped out of the bathtub, letting Huanxi dry her with a clean towel. After her hair was wrung dry, she lay down on the bed.

If Song Ling didn’t want her near, then she would have to find another way.

She couldn’t cry every day to soften his heart. Tears were a weapon once, but too many times would just make him annoyed.

The storybooks said that things touched by a "medicinal guide" could also nourish the body. A thought suddenly occurred to Shu You.

If she couldn’t get close to him, maybe she could take something he had touched.

For example, clothes he had worn, or...

Shu You looked at the wet marks on the floor that hadn’t dried yet, lost in thought.

...

Shu You decided to act immediately. She deliberately chose a time when Song Ling was usually in the Qiyun Hall and sneaked toward the small courtyard she had visited the day before.

With a creak, the door pushed open easily.

It wasn’t even locked. Perfect for her.

Shu You stood at the steps, hesitating. Excluding the room where they had eaten yesterday, there were three other rooms. Which one was Song Ling’s?

Time was tight, and the task was urgent. Shu You headed straight for the central and largest room.

She pushed the door, no luck, it was locked.

Shu You couldn’t push it open, so she immediately went to look for a window, planning to climb in. But the window was also tightly shut and couldn’t be opened.

Since this room wouldn’t open, she would check the others.

She looked around to make sure no one was there, then carefully made her way to the back of the side room. She saw a window propped open with a small gap, and her heart leapt with joy. She bit her lip and carefully climbed in without making a sound.

The room was very spacious but had few furnishings. In the center was a square bathtub.

Shu You was somewhat shocked. There was actually a bathtub built in here, how extravagant.

Just how rich was this Song Ling?

Moreover, there was no one around now, but the tub was still misty. Shu You crouched down and reached out to touch it, it was still hot.

The tub couldn’t be constantly heated, so either hot water had just been added, or he had just finished bathing. Thinking of this, Shu You was suddenly startled. She didn’t dare think further and decided to quickly take something of Song Ling’s and leave.

She noticed a set of white clothes not far away, like an undershirt. She picked it up and held it to her chest, planning to climb out the window. Suddenly, she heard the sound of a door opening, and footsteps were approaching.

Oh no! Shu You was so frightened that she was at a loss, her mind blank. If she was discovered, she was doomed.

chapters.title: Turns Out He Has Fair Skin
chapters.content:
She had to find a place to hide quickly!

Shu You’s breathing trembled, her chest aching from her rapid heartbeat. She tightly clutched the undershirt in her arms, her eyes darting to the partition by the curtain. She stood up and quickly hid behind it.

The footsteps stopped by the tub. Shu You held her breath, not daring to look at who had come, shrinking behind the partition without moving.

After waiting a while without hearing any more footsteps, Shu You swallowed hard. Why wasn’t he continuing to walk?

Had she already been discovered?

She cautiously peeked her head out to see what was happening, but as soon as she saw, she quickly retracted it.

Shouldn’t Song Ling be in Qiyun Hall at this time?

Why had he suddenly come back to bathe?

Shu You’s mind repeatedly replayed the scene she had just witnessed: the clothes slipping off, revealing smooth, fair, and even skin.

So Song Ling actually had fair skin, and it was quite good-looking.

At this thought, Shu You silently gave her own cheek a light slap, trying to wake herself up.

What was she thinking!

Peeping at someone bathing was not the act of a gentleman. Shu You realized this a little belatedly. But wait, she was a woman, not a gentleman, so maybe it was okay?

Shu You pursed her lips and turned her head again. She could only see the man’s back, a beautiful pair of shoulder blades. His lower body was submerged in the tub as he walked deeper, the water gradually rising to his chest.

A hint of regret flashed in her eyes. If only she hadn’t looked away earlier. Now she couldn’t see anything.

Disappointed, she leaned against the partition, listening to the splashing water. Shu You was bored. How long did it take for a man to bathe?

It should be over soon, right? She thought silently.

After two quarters of an hour, Shu You’s legs were numb from standing. Why was he taking so long? Was there that much dirt to scrub off?

Shu You couldn’t help but rotate her ankles to relieve the stiffness, praying that Song Ling would finish quickly so she could leave.

As she closed her eyes, she accidentally bumped into something, causing a loud *bang*. She immediately froze. Even though it hurt, she didn’t dare cry out.

The sound of the water suddenly stopped. A sharp, hawk-like gaze shot directly at Shu You. The man’s voice was cold enough to freeze someone to death.

"Who’s there? Come out."

Xiao Ling looked toward the source of the noise, his body tense like a drawn bowstring. Although assassins hadn’t been as common in recent years as in the past, he had never let his guard down.

His hand reached for a mechanism in the pool. As soon as the assassin appeared, he would make sure they had no way out.

The screen by the curtain moved slightly. Xiao Ling’s fingertip had already touched the button. All he needed was a light press, and the assassin would be separated from their head.

But when he saw the head peeking out from behind the curtain, his eyebrows instantly furrowed. A surge of anger welled up inside him, and his finger unconsciously moved away from the mechanism.

"Why is it you? What are you doing here?"

Shu You lowered her head, forcing a dry smile, her expression stiff. She raised her hand to greet Song Ling. "Hi, what a coincidence."

Her gaze fell on the man’s well-defined chest and abdomen, and her face suddenly turned red. She wished she could find a crack in the ground to hide in.

She had come to steal clothes and ended up seeing him bathe. This was too embarrassing.

Xiao Ling’s eyebrows twisted. He sank his body deeper into the water. His usually cold voice now carried suppressed anger. "Explain."

Half of her body was exposed, and the white undershirt she was holding in front of her chest looked familiar. He glanced at the tray on the chair, which was missing an undershirt.

Xiao Ling instantly understood most of the situation. This woman was indeed bold, she had actually come to steal his clothes and even peeked at him bathing.

Thinking that she had seen his bare body clearly, his face flushed red and white with embarrassment. It was simply outrageous!

At twenty-one years old, except for his childhood, Xiao Ling didn’t like having attendants around when he bathed. Thus, very few people had seen his private parts.

Now she had seen it all.

How could there be a woman so bold and reckless? Unable to win his heart, she sought other means.

He had truly underestimated her. She looked soft and weak, yet everything she did was shocking.

Shu You hesitated, her face red as blood. She stammered, "Song... Young Master Song, I..."

"I actually..." She looked at the white undershirt in her hands, on the verge of tears. "If I said I was short on clothes and came to borrow one from you, would you believe me?"

The man gave a sarcastic smile, his eyes fixed tightly on her. "Do you think I would?"

Such a poor excuse. Who would believe that?

As expected, he was angry. His exquisite eyebrows were tinged with resentment, visible even from a distance.

"Actually, after a few encounters with you, Young Master Song, I have already developed admiration for you. I wanted to see you but was afraid you would find me annoying."

Shu You glanced quickly at the man in the water, only his fair shoulders and neck visible. A thought struck her, and she took a detour, hoping to escape today’s predicament.

If she told the truth, she might not leave this room today.

Sure enough, a flicker of understanding passed through Xiao Ling’s eyes. So she admired him deeply, which was why she had such impure thoughts. Seeing the girl in front of him, blushing to the point of fainting, he turned his face away, the suppressed anger in his voice dissipating slightly.

"Get out."

Right now, he wasn’t wearing any clothes, so it wasn’t convenient to talk to her. Thinking of how she had seen him naked, Xiao Ling’s cheeks, already flushed from the steam, deepened in color. He turned his face away, no longer looking at her.

Shu You felt a surge of joy upon hearing this. He was going to let her go. She nodded like a chick pecking at rice and prepared to move quickly.

This was too embarrassing.

As she passed the tub, she didn’t dare look at him, afraid of seeing something she shouldn’t.

The wet tiles echoed with light footsteps. Xiao Ling saw her head almost buried in her chest, still clutching the white undershirt.

Why was she still holding onto it? Did she really want to take it with her? He spoke up in time to remind her: "Put down the undershirt in your hand before you leave."

Shu You was already nervous, and her only thought was to leave quickly. She hadn’t expected him to suddenly speak as she passed him. Startled, she slipped.

*Splash!* She fell into the tub.

The tub was very deep. Shu You couldn’t swim, and no matter how she tried, her feet couldn’t touch the bottom. She flailed in the water, creating splashes.

This was it. No one could save her now.

Just as Shu You thought she was about to drown, a sturdy arm pulled her up. As if grabbing a lifesaving straw, she clutched him tightly, refusing to let go, her arms wrapped around his neck.

She desperately gasped for air, her breath scorching the skin it touched.

A force tried to push her away, but Shu You, from some unknown source of strength, held onto him tightly, pressing close to him. She was completely soaked, her eyes filled with fear and helplessness, her pitiful look making it hard for anyone to push her away.

"Let go," Xiao Ling lowered his head, glanced once, and didn’t dare look again. The girl in his arms, now soaked, had her thin clothes become somewhat transparent, faintly revealing a pink ribbon. With every breath, he could feel a different texture against him.

Soft, tender, and wet.

"I won’t," Shu You, after her initial shock, fearlessly continued to hold him, still not fully recovered. She lay on the man’s shoulder, panting softly.

Her voice was soft, carrying a hint of grievance and coquettishness, with a thousand twists and turns. It was so soft that it numbed half of Xiao Ling’s body.

Under the double stimulation, an involuntary reaction stirred in his body.

chapters.title: Where Are You Looking?
chapters.content:
The steam beneath the bath seemed to rise like a coiled dragon, layer upon layer of heat surging upward, steaming Shu You’s cheeks a flushed red, her entire body tinged with a faint pink.

As she lay draped over the man, gradually regaining her strength, she began to realize something was amiss. Her hands clung to his broad shoulders, her palms sliding over smooth skin, and the collarbone before her eyes was slender and refined.

A droplet of water slid downward, the dark mole on his skin unmistakably clear.

Shu You stared blankly as the water droplet traced down his chest and abdomen. Just as she was about to look lower, her chin was lifted by a large hand. The man’s voice was displeased: "Where are you looking?"

Her mind went blank with a sudden *bang*, her face burning red as if she were a boiled shrimp. Instinctively, she tried to loosen her grip, her body sliding down a few inches, only to immediately cling to him again, even tighter than before.

As she leaned in, she suddenly heard a deep, pleasant hum from the man’s throat. Shu You didn’t dare move, terrified she might touch somewhere she shouldn’t.

Neither of them spoke. Shu You turned her head slightly toward the shore, wanting to ask him to put her down. But the moment she uttered a syllable, she was startled by her own voice.

"Song... Gongzi..." Even she felt a flush of shame at the sound. Sure enough, as soon as the words left her mouth, the chest beside her cheek rose and fell sharply, tensing even more.

Shu You instantly dared not speak again. Her mind was in chaos, as if two little people were fighting inside her.

The white little person told her to let go, while the black little person urged her to take this perfect opportunity and sleep with him.

Though only a few moments had passed, Shu You’s mind had already spun through countless schemes. Just as she hesitated, something poked her waist.

Shu You stiffened. *He’s not wearing clothes... so what is this...?*

She didn’t dare think further, burying her head in the man’s embrace, too afraid to lift it.

A splash of water sounded in her ears. Her waist was pulled in, lifted higher, and the man’s arms slipped beneath her knees, steadying her in his hold.

"Close your eyes. Don’t look around," the man said. His voice wasn’t as cold as usual, it carried a faint rasp, deep and magnetic.

Shu You softly hummed in response, tightly shutting her eyes and burying herself against his neck. She didn’t dare glance around. The patch of skin where their foreheads touched was scorching hot.

She didn’t know where she was being placed, perhaps a low stool. The next moment, a piece of clothing, faintly scented with sandalwood, was draped over her head.

"Don’t move," the man said just as Shu You was about to push it away. She immediately dropped her hands and sat obediently.

Xiao Ling glanced at the girl not far away. She looked well-behaved but was far from honest. He picked up the discarded clothes nearby to cover her eyes, preventing her from peeking.

After wiping the water from his body, he habitually put on his undershirt. Pausing for a moment, he turned back to look at the pale, translucent clothes floating in the pool. A flicker of helplessness passed through his eyes. He dressed quickly in the remaining clothes.

The girl was already soaked through. If she wore her own clothes back, she’d surely catch a cold. He frowned for a moment, then left with a single sentence:

"Wait here."

Shu You responded, and when she heard him leave, she quietly lifted the clothing to watch his retreating figure. The door opened and then closed.

Xiao Ling walked to the main house and called out to Xing Jue at the doorway.

Xing Jue immediately emerged from the small kitchen, taking a few steps to stand before him, bowing slightly. "Dianxia."

"Go find a set of women’s clothes. Quickly."

Xing Jue was stunned for a moment, not reacting in time, as if he’d misheard. But when he looked up at his lord’s unyielding face, he immediately replied, "Yes, this subordinate will see to it."

Within moments, he disappeared from the courtyard. Though Dianxia hadn’t explained why, there must be a reason.

Xiao Ling pushed open the door, changed into a fresh undershirt, and casually picked up a crescent-colored robe, retracing his steps back.

Inside the room, Shu You heard the door open and immediately put down the clothes, lowering her head to fidget with her fingers.

"Put the clothes on quickly," Xiao Ling said, looking at her soaked dress clinging tightly to her body, water droplets trailing down the hem. He subconsciously cleared his throat, looked up, turned around, and walked out, standing by the door to wait.

Once he left, Shu You lifted the clothes from her head in one motion. She glanced toward the door, where a figure stood vaguely outside. She stood up and removed her wet clothes.

But then she hit a snag. Normally, it was Huanxi who helped her dress, and besides, this was clearly men’s clothing, it didn’t fit her figure at all. Wearing it made her look like a child sneaking into someone else’s clothes.

She adjusted the lapels and looked toward the man at the door, taking a few steps forward to lightly knock. "Song Gongzi, could you come in for a moment?"

Xiao Ling assumed she was already dressed. When he opened the door and saw her current state, his spine stiffened, and he turned away. "Why aren’t you dressed properly?"

The clothes hung loosely on her, and as Xiao Ling looked down, he could even see her collarbone beneath the neckline.

"I *am* dressed," Shu You said, awkwardly scratching her face. "I don’t know how to tie the knots on these clothes. Could you help me?"

After all, these were his clothes, he must know how to wear them. And it was just helping with a knot, not helping her get dressed.

Xiao Ling closed his eyes and sighed deeply. He took a few steps forward, turned his face away, and in a few quick motions, tied her belt. His voice was hoarse, barely audible. "Done."

He moved so fast that Shu You didn’t even see how he did it. A soft smile tugged at her lips. "Thank you, Song Gongzi."

After saying that, she looked toward the courtyard gate, pressing her lips together. *Could she leave now?*

While the man was still flustered, his eartips still red, she should go quickly.

Otherwise, once he came to his senses about what had happened today, she’d be in big trouble.

Recalling Xiao Ling’s cold face when they first met, Shu You’s heart trembled. This wasn’t a small matter, she might get scolded until she was drenched in blood.

"I’ll take my leave then," Shu You said, picking up her clothes and planning to slip away after saying goodbye. She stepped over the threshold toward the gate.

"Are you just going to leave like this?" The man stretched out his arm, blocking her path, his face disapproving.

Shu You looked down at herself and didn’t see anything wrong. The clothes were a bit too big and didn’t fit well, but at least they covered her body.

She could just be careful on the way back to avoid being seen. It wasn’t a big problem.

Xiao Ling’s face darkened as he noticed the fair skin exposed at her collar. His left arm remained still, and he turned his face away. "Wait here. I’ve had Xing Jue fetch a set of women’s clothes. He’ll be back soon."

Shu You oh-ed, looking at him and then at herself. *Were they just supposed to stand here like this?*

Her shoes were full of water, and the dampness was unbearable. She took a few steps forward and tugged at his sleeve.

Shu You saw that he didn’t seem as angry anymore. She tilted her head up at him. "Song Gongzi, are you still mad?"

"Please don’t be angry, okay?"

Every time her mother, Ye Yun, was angry, this trick worked. Once she softened, Shu You would press her advantage, hugging her wrist and shaking it gently, and all her anger would vanish.

The man’s lips pressed into a straight line, his profile stubborn and cold, not looking at her or speaking.

Shu You couldn’t tell what he meant. Was he still waiting for her to coax him, or did he not want to hear her speak?

She tried stepping closer, hooking his little finger through his sleeve and gently shaking it. Softly, she said, "Forgive me, please."

She didn’t dare bring up the matter of peeking at him bathing again, afraid he’d remember and get angry.

---

chapters.title: Bring Out the Heavy Artillery!
chapters.content:
Xiao Ling’s reddened ears suddenly twitched twice, and his heart trembled, a wave of bitterness rising within him. He didn’t know what this feeling was, it was unfamiliar.

A rare sense of helplessness filled his heart. He wanted to tell her to stop acting so coy, but when he glanced at those pitiful, pleading eyes, the words stuck in his throat, unable to come out.

The two of them stood frozen, neither speaking.

Shu You saw that he still wasn’t talking and knew he definitely didn’t want to forgive her. Her usual tricks didn’t work on him.

This man was truly cold-hearted. Shu You felt a pang of defeat. Every time she took the initiative, he showed no special reaction. It seemed Song Gongzi didn’t like her type at all.

All the physical contact they’d had these past few days had been for nothing.

Shu You lowered her gaze, her thoughts spinning wildly. Since he didn’t like her, and she only wanted his body, she needed to find a way to get it done quickly.

As the storybooks always said, once a man had a taste, wouldn’t he come back for more?

Twenty times sounded like a lot, but when she thought about it, it didn’t seem all that many.

If she seduced him more diligently, maybe she wouldn’t even need two months before she could return home.

And since he didn’t like her, that was an advantage, it meant he wouldn’t cling to her afterward. They could treat it as a dream, and since they wouldn’t see each other again in the future, it wouldn’t matter.

She had never seduced a man before, and her acting was terrible. This time, she’d even been caught stealing his clothes. He must be annoyed with her. The idea that he might actually like her was absurd.

Her long lashes lowered, but her eyes darted beneath them, quickly sorting through her thoughts. Since her previous plan to win his heart hadn’t worked, it was time to bring out the heavy artillery.

She needed to find time to visit an apothecary. A love potion? Incense? Or something else?

She had money, so she could buy everything in one go. At worst, she’d try each one, surely one of them would work.

Lost in thought, Shu You didn’t notice the man’s gaze flickering toward her from time to time, as if he wanted to say something but held back.

The sound of rapid footsteps outside broke the silence. Xing Jue arrived, carrying a tray with clothes and even shoes and socks prepared.

As he was about to bow, he caught a glimpse of the figure at the door. The moment he recognized her, his own lord blocked his view completely, leaving nothing visible.

Xing Jue’s pupils widened in shock, his lips parting slightly. For a moment, he forgot what to say next.

*What had he just seen?!*

Miss Jiang was wearing his lord’s clothes! And the two of them had been in the bathing chamber the whole time. His lord had even sent him to fetch a set of women’s clothes.

Why would he need women’s clothes unless the old ones were no longer wearable... which meant...

What they had done was obvious. His lord had acted with surprising speed, which truly startled Xing Jue.

Xiao Ling took the tray and glanced at him, saying in a deep voice, "Leave."

Xing Jue nodded blankly, his expression dazed as he turned to leave, not forgetting to close the door behind him.

He felt like he was dreaming. His lord, who was usually distant and never involved in romantic affairs, now had a woman he favored.

The clothes were carried by the man’s arm and presented to Shu You. She took them and softly said, "Thank you, Gongzi."

She shuffled toward the screen inside the room. After hearing the door open and close again, she changed out of her current clothes.

Though she hadn’t seen how he tied the knot, Shu You didn’t dare bother him again. She clumsily tied a bow herself, finished dressing, and decided to leave.

Shu You pushed open the door. Song Gongzi was nowhere to be seen, only Xing Jue stood with his back to her in the courtyard.

He heard the sound but didn’t turn immediately, instead asking politely, "Miss Jiang, are you ready?"

Shu You softly hummed and walked toward him. Song Gongzi really didn’t want to acknowledge her, he’d disappeared in the time it took to change clothes. He wouldn’t even spare her a glance, let alone say goodbye.

Her resolve deepened. She needed to go down the mountain as soon as possible.

"Miss Jiang, I’ll take you out," Xing Jue said, turning toward her and walking over to lead the way, his gaze subtly studying the delicate young woman beside him.

They weren’t far apart, but Xing Jue could faintly catch a familiar scent from her, the unmistakable sandalwood fragrance.

*This is serious.* It seemed his guess was correct. Miss Jiang would soon enter the Eastern Palace as its mistress. He just didn’t know what position his lord would give her.

Though Miss Jiang wasn’t from a noble family, her background was clean.

Investigating her background had been his own order, and he knew it inside and out.

The girl beside him hung her head, looking pitiful.

Xing Jue sighed silently. *Of course she’s upset.* Her lover had disappeared the moment she changed clothes, leaving her alone. How could she be happy?

"Miss Jiang, my lord had urgent business and left. It’s not that he didn’t want to say goodbye to you."

Xing Jue spoke the truth. Just now, an Eastern Palace guard had suddenly appeared outside, summoning his lord away and leaving him to wait here.

Hearing the man’s reassurance, Shu You ah-ed and lifted her head, pulling herself from her thoughts.

She hadn’t been thinking about Song Gongzi at all, she was just worried about the distance between Changshan Temple and the city, wondering how she’d get down the mountain later.

Shu You studied the young servant several times. He had clear brows and bright eyes, looking extremely kind. She knew he meant well, assuming she was upset because Song Gongzi had left. A light smile touched her eyes. "Thank you. What’s your name?"

"This servant is called Xing Jue, the *xing* of stars, the *jue* of jade pendant."

"What a nice name," Shu You said, her almond-shaped eyes curving. The name suited him well. "Can I call you Xing Jue from now on?"

Xing Jue nodded, his tone growing more respectful. He opened the courtyard gate and stood to the side. "As you wish, Miss."

This was likely his future mistress, he couldn’t afford to be negligent.

Shu You smiled and nodded, about to turn and leave when she noticed he was following her, not staying behind. She asked in confusion, "Does Xing Jue have something urgent to attend to?"

"I’ll escort Miss Jiang back," Xing Jue shook his head. His lord had ordered him to safely send her back before leaving, and he was simply following orders.

The journey was long, and it wouldn’t be safe for the young lady to return alone. His lord had been thorough in his arrangements.

Shu You shook her head upon hearing this. *He’s so considerate, far better than that Song Gongzi.* But she knew the way and could return on her own. "Thank you, but I can go back by myself. I know the way."

A place this big, and Xing Jue was the only one here, who knew how many tasks he had in a day?

If Song Gongzi disliked her, and he found out Xing Jue had neglected his duties to escort her, it would cause trouble.

Better not.

She refused repeatedly, and Xing Jue didn’t insist further. However, after she walked far enough that her figure was out of sight, he quietly followed, only leaving once he saw her enter her own small courtyard.

Huanxi was in the courtyard washing and drying clothes. When she saw her mistress return, she called out, but the next moment, she sensed something was wrong and immediately stepped forward. Seeing Shu You’s clothes, her eyes widened. "Miss, what is this?"

Shu You followed her gaze to her own attire and sighed lightly, waving her hand. "Ah, it’s nothing. My clothes just got wet, so I changed into another set."

"I’m fine."

She walked straight into the house and sat at the round table, pulling a white undershirt from her sleeve and tossing it onto the table. She pondered silently: *Would this still work if it’s washed?*

This was the undershirt she had secretly stuffed into her sleeve when no one was in the room, she had seen Xiao Ling take it off with her own eyes.

"Miss!" Huanxi followed her inside, and upon seeing her actions, she was left speechless. "Where did this clothing come from?"

Shu You propped her cheek in her hand, her eyes curving into slits with a smile. She picked up the clothing with her fingertips. "Stole it."

chapters.title: Money Can Make the Devil Turn the Millstone
chapters.content:
Seeing Xianxi staring blankly, Shu You burst into a soft laugh. She grabbed a handful of her undergarment, and where her skin touched the fabric, a tingling sensation spread, slowly crawling up her arm.

Shu You pondered for a moment. It seemed that the clothes that had been in contact with the person did have some effect, though not as strong as direct contact.

Still, something was better than nothing.

Fortunately, she had escaped a disaster today. Song Ling hadn’t held it against her, but Shu You didn’t want to see him for the next few days.

She would wait a few days until he wasn’t so angry before going to see him again. That way, she wouldn’t have to lower her head and coax him like today.

Coaxing him was one thing, but it was useless. Shu You sighed, her shoulders drooping in defeat.

"Xianxi, take this garment and wash it," Shu You said, dropping the undergarment before pouring herself a cup of water. She rested her chin in her hand, lost in thought, her brows furrowing and relaxing as if troubled by something.

"Miss, has something happened?" Xianxi noticed her tone was off and stopped in her tracks, the garment still in her hand.

Shu You shifted her gaze to her, looking at the legs hidden under her skirt with worry. "Xianxi, I want to go down the mountain."

Changshan Temple was so far from the city. They only had their own two legs, and it was uncertain if they could make it even if they walked from sunrise to sunset.

Most importantly, they didn’t know the way. The previous two times, they had the carriage from the mansion. This time...

Xianxi let out a cheerful "hai" upon hearing this, her eyes sparkling as if this were a trivial matter. "So Miss wants to go down the mountain? That’s easy. Leave it to me."

"You have a carriage?" Shu You straightened up, her eyes flashing with surprise and delight. She leaned in, grabbing Xianxi’s hands, her voice soft and cheerful. "Tell me the truth!"

"I met several people when I went to the vegetarian hall a few days ago. The widow living in the neighboring courtyard has a carriage. It only takes a little silver to arrange."

Shu You’s heart leapt with joy, but she remained cautious. "Is she trustworthy? Does she know our identities?"

"Miss, rest assured. I am very careful. I only told her we were staying temporarily and nothing else," Xianxi replied, her voice steady. She smiled and made a gesture with her fingers, rubbing her thumb, index, and middle fingers together. "We have money."

"Money can make the devil turn the millstone."

The two burst into laughter. This gesture had been taught to her by Shu You herself.

Shu You’s eyes filled with admiration. Her maid was reliable. After careful consideration, she set the date for their descent. Her voice was cheerful. "Then let’s go tomorrow. We’ll stay down the mountain for a few days and rent a carriage to come back."

Xianxi agreed with a smile, curtsied, and turned to leave the room to wash the clothes.

...

It had rained in the middle of the night, and the air was filled with a damp mist. The grass and trees beside the corridor still retained droplets of water.

Xiao Ling walked slowly past the corridor. From a distance, he saw the main gate of Qiyun Hall. As he passed the stone pillar, he instinctively lowered his gaze. There was no one behind the pillar.

Usually, the girl would sit there waiting for him.

It had been two days, and Shu You had not appeared again. He didn’t know if something had happened or if there was another reason.

Xiao Ling coldly averted his gaze and entered the hall without closing the door completely. Whether she came or not was none of his concern. It was better if she didn’t come.

That clingy person wasn’t here, so he could finally have some peace. He hadn’t forgotten about her peeping at him while he bathed. Who knew what other bad ideas she was brewing.

Xiao Ling knelt in front of the prayer mat as usual, closing his eyes and murmuring. His clear voice echoed softly in the hall.

Everything was as usual, no different from before, except that the speed at which Xiao Ling turned his prayer beads had increased slightly.

Suddenly, footsteps echoed outside the door, growing louder. Xiao Ling’s prayer beads paused for a moment before continuing.

With a creak, the heavy wooden door was pushed open, and the footsteps approached him. Xiao Ling assumed it was Shu You again. A slight smirk tugged at his lips, and he didn’t even lift his head. "Who allowed you to come in?"

She had entered without knocking, growing bolder and more unruly.

A deep, aged voice resonated in the hall. "This old monk has come uninvited to disturb Your Highness. Please do not blame me."

It wasn’t her.

Xiao Ling turned his head and looked up to see the white-haired Abbot Liaochen, who cupped his hands in greeting. Xiao Ling’s lips curled into a faint smile. "Abbot, what brings you here?"

Abbot Liaochen had kind eyes and a gentle voice. "I passed by Qiyun Hall today and saw the door was open, so I came in to greet you. How have you been lately, Your Highness?"

"Same as always," Xiao Ling replied, lowering his head to continue chanting. His tone was calm and indifferent.

"If that is the case, this old monk will not disturb you further," Abbot Liaochen said with a smile, not minding his coldness. He clasped his hands together, turned, and left. As he stepped over the threshold, he left behind a sentence that scattered with the wind.

"If Your Highness’s mind is unsettled, perhaps you should go out for a walk."

Xiao Ling was slightly stunned after hearing this. He looked at the bodhi prayer beads in his hand, his eyelashes casting a shadow as he pondered.

The unease in his heart, which he couldn’t explain, had been seen through by the Abbot in just a few words. In that brief moment, his thoughts spun endlessly.

Why was his mind unsettled? Was it because Shu You hadn’t come for the past two days?

This thought arose and was immediately dismissed by Xiao Ling. How could that be? They had only met a few times.

Could it be that her clumsy attempts at seduction had made him like her?

Xiao Ling let out a soft scoff. It must be because of those old fools in the court. What did it have to do with Shu You?

After Abbot Liaochen’s visit, Xiao Ling lost the mood to continue chanting. He turned and walked back to his small courtyard.

Xing Jue, in the small kitchen with the door and windows open, saw his master walking straight back to the main house without stopping. He felt a pang of curiosity.

He looked up at the sky. It was still early. Why had his master returned?

But he didn’t dwell on it. He focused on using the fan to carefully tend to the medicine pot in front of him. He couldn’t afford to neglect it.

Half an hour later, Xing Jue carried the tray and knocked on the door. After hearing a "come in" from inside, he pushed the door open.

"Your Highness, it’s time for your medicine."

Xiao Ling was sitting at the desk, copying the Heart Sutra. Without lifting his head, he said indifferently, "Put it down."

"Yes," Xing Jue carefully placed the tray on the corner of the desk. White porcelain bowls continuously emitted wisps of steam. He didn’t urge him to drink, but stood silently by the side, staring at the steam in a daze.

His master had been poisoned since birth.

The late empress had not noticed during her pregnancy. After giving birth to His Highness, she passed away a few years later.

This poison had followed him from childhood to adulthood. Countless precious tonics and good medicines had been tried, but none could cure it. They could only suppress it.

At first, he only needed to take the medicine three times a month. Now, as the medicine’s effect gradually weakened, he had to take it more frequently, every three days. What if the medicine stopped working in the future?

Xing Jue was worried. He had once privately asked the imperial physician if there were any other methods. The white-haired physician had shaken his head and sighed.

"His Highness’s body has been soaked in medicine for a long time. The medicine’s effect on him is gradually diminishing and will only become shorter."

"You should advise His Highness to find a yin-deficient woman as soon as possible."

Yes, His Highness’s condition wasn’t completely hopeless. As long as he harmonized yin and yang with a yin-deficient woman and took medicine, the poison could be gradually eliminated.

But His Highness was unwilling.

Xing Jue had heard some reasons for his unwillingness and silently shook his head.

But the pain of the poison flaring up was no joke.

He had once seen His Highness during a flare-up, lying in bed with his entire body red, almost fainting from the pain. It had taken a whole night for him to recover.

Xing Jue wasn’t lacking in persuasion, but when those bloodshot eyes glanced over, he couldn’t say a word.

chapters.title: They Finally Came to the Right Place
chapters.content:
His Highness was strong-willed, sharp, and brooked no argument.

His Highness was a man of strong opinions. As a servant, Xing Jue didn’t dare to advise too much. He could only wait for the day His Highness changed his mind.

But things were different now.

A woman had appeared by His Highness’s side, and she was a woman who could have intimate contact with him.

No wonder Xing Jue was excited. His hands, hidden in his sleeves, were clenched white. His Highness had never had contact with other women before. Many noble ladies had "coincidentally" met him, but His Highness had never spared them a glance.

He recalled the last time he saw Miss Jiang in the bathhouse wearing their master’s clothes. This meant he no longer rejected women.

Harmonizing yin and yang with a yin-deficient woman was no longer a dream.

Life suddenly had hope. He needed to find the right person now so that she could be used when the time came, Xing Jue thought.

If he didn’t drink the medicine soon, it would get cold. Xing Jue hesitated whether to remind him, but His Highness was copying the scripture. Interrupting him abruptly might displease him.

He sighed silently again. Other medicines didn’t work, only this one did.

Moreover, the fire poison was too severe. Other poisons and medicines had no effect on His Highness. This was perhaps the only advantage.

Xiao Ling put down his pen, picked up the porcelain bowl, and drank it in one go. The unease in his heart dissipated, and he returned to his usual calm.

Xing Jue stepped forward to clean up without saying a word. His Highness was irritated and liked to copy the Heart Sutra. Although he didn’t know why he was upset, it was better not to touch this bad luck. He quietly retreated.

Two chattering sparrows perched on the open window sill, lingering for a long time, attracting Xiao Ling’s attention from his desk.

The pair of sparrows moved together, their heads occasionally coming together as if whispering, like a pair of lovers who shared everything.

Xiao Ling watched the sparrows, lost in thought. For some reason, he thought of Shu You again. She always tirelessly talked in his ear. If she didn’t get a response, she would keep acting coy to get him to reply.

Sometimes, when he responded, he would catch a glimpse of her expression, joy, delight, her eyes filled with smiles.

She must have liked it a lot, otherwise she wouldn’t have clung to him every time.

Where had she gone these past two days?

At this thought, Xiao Ling’s expression suddenly turned cold. Why was he thinking of her again?

He exhaled a turbid breath, picked up his pen again, and continued copying the Heart Sutra, trying to banish her image from his mind.

...

Main street of the capital city.

Shu You had been strolling around the city with Xianxi for two days. Their feet were sore. They had visited every large pharmacy and asked about the medicine.

She had asked openly and directly for that kind of medicine.

"Do you have that kind of thing?"

"A medicine that can... induce estrus."

"No, we don’t," the shopkeeper said with a strange expression, his eyes continuously scanning the two of them. "This is a reputable pharmacy."

Every shop said they didn’t have it, which made Shu You very disheartened. She didn’t have much time. Her body might return to its original state at any moment. She randomly found a restaurant, booked a private room for lunch, and took the opportunity to rest her feet.

"Miss, why are you looking for... that kind of thing?" Xianxi’s face was flushed, her eyes full of confusion. After hesitating for a long time, she finally asked the question.

Xianxi stood next to Shu You, using a handkerchief to carefully wipe the sweat from her pale face. The sun was strong today, and she didn’t want her to sweat and catch a cold.

Shu You didn’t intend to hide it from her. Anyway, she couldn’t hide it. She just needed her to keep it a secret.

"Of course, it’s for intimate matters," Shu You slowly drank a cup of tea and raised an eyebrow at her. "Have you noticed that your miss has been looking much better recently?"

Xianxi nodded, her eyes flashing with some certainty.
