"Come here," Shu You smiled and beckoned her. When she came closer, Shu You whispered in her ear, telling her everything she had learned from the storybooks.

In the marquis’s mansion, apart from her parents and brothers, Xianxi was the person she trusted the most. Telling her would also make things more convenient in the future.

Xianxi’s face suddenly turned as red as a cooked shrimp. She stammered, "Miss!"

This kind of bizarre thing was simply...

Xianxi didn’t believe it at first, but she had seen that her miss’s complexion had indeed improved a lot recently. They had walked together for two days without her panting. She believed it a little.

"So Miss came to Changshan Temple just to..." Xianxi swallowed the rest of the words in her throat, looking embarrassed.

Shu You snapped her fingers, her beautiful eyes full of cunning. "You guessed right. This secret is known only to you. You must keep it well for me."

"If this trip is successful, your miss’s body will be able to recover its health."

If it really worked, the prophecy of not living past eighteen would be like an inflated balloon, one poke and it would burst. Her family wouldn’t have to worry anymore.

Xianxi also thought of this. Her eyes gradually turned red, and she slowly nodded. "I know, Miss. I will keep the secret and help you recover your health."

Shu You achieved her goal. Her eyes smiled into crescents, and she stretched out her little finger to hook with Xianxi’s.

After eating, she started to worry again. The pharmacies definitely had it, but they were unwilling to sell it. What could she do?

As Shu You was resting her chin, lost in thought, a series of coquettish laughter from outside the private room reached her ears.

"Sir, come over."

"One moment of spring night is worth a thousand gold. Don’t waste it."

The fleeting thoughts in her mind were quickly captured by Shu You. As if enlightened, she stood up, and a realization spread throughout her body.

Reputable pharmacies wouldn’t sell it, but there were other places that would!

She went to the window and looked at the brothel across the street. Several young women sat on the railing, waving their silk handkerchiefs.

Shu You’s eyes sparkled as if with stars. She smiled sweetly, revealing her dimples, and leaned against the door, calling out, "Sisters, could you come over for a moment?"

The women across the street heard someone calling them. They looked over and saw a delicate and pretty girl. After exchanging puzzled glances and seeing her take out several taels of silver, they got up and came over.

"Sit, sit," Shu You gestured for Xianxi to pour tea for the two women. The private room was filled with a strong fragrance. She spoke kindly, "I just want to ask you sisters a few questions."

"After I ask, this silver is yours." On the table were six taels of silver, a full sixty taels.

"Miss, please ask," said a woman in a green gauze skirt, looking a bit more composed as she shifted her gaze from the silver.

Shu You had been out for two days without any results. She got straight to the point. "Do you sisters know where to buy... estrus medicine?"

They had seen and experienced a lot in this area and must have many connections.

The two women, one in red and one in green, exchanged a glance, their eyes showing some confusion. They hadn’t expected this girl, who looked like she came from a good family, to ask such a question.

"I know," said the woman in the green gauze skirt, clearing her throat several times, her eyes fixed on the silver in front of her. "There’s a shop on North Street that specializes in selling such things. There are many varieties. Our madam goes there to stock up."

Shu You’s pupils lit up slightly, unable to hide her joy. "Thank you, sisters. This silver is yours."

It was so easy. Asking them had indeed worked.

After they left, Shu You pulled Xianxi toward North Street, her eyes constantly scanning the signs. Suddenly, she stopped. She had found it!

Shu You looked up at the sign above her head: Ziyi Pavilion. The name was quite bold.

She pulled Xianxi inside. The light inside the shop was much dimmer than outside, and there was no one guarding it. It was quiet.

The two of them, hand in hand, looked at the items displayed on both sides, their faces gradually turning crimson.

There were all kinds of items: exquisite chains, red oil candles, and variously shaped...

Shu You’s face turned completely red, but her eyes were filled with growing excitement. They had finally come to the right place.

"Is anyone here?"

chapters.title: A Man of Contradictions
chapters.content:
After waiting a few moments with no response, Shu You gathered her courage and called out again, "Excuse me, is anyone there?"

Still, no one answered.

Was the shop really left unattended with the door wide open?

Shu You and Huanxi exchanged puzzled glances, unsure whether to leave or continue waiting. Then, a voice, soft and enchanting beyond measure, reached them before its owner appeared.

"Coming, coming, honored guest, please wait."

Shu You turned toward the sound and saw a woman in red emerge from behind a curtain. Her features were strikingly beautiful, her fox-like eyes shimmering with allure, and every movement exuded charm.

"Excuse me, are you the shopkeeper?" Shu You's eyes widened with a hint of admiration. Surprisingly, it was a woman, and her tension eased slightly. "I'm here to buy something."

The fox-eyed woman scrutinized the two young girls before her. The one in front clearly seemed to be the mistress. It was quite unusual for a respectable young lady to come to a place like this, and a flicker of curiosity and interest stirred within her.

"What would the honored guest like to purchase?"

Her shop specialized in items for intimate pleasure between men and women. This young girl had quite the nerve.

Shu You glanced at the open door behind her and lowered her voice, "Shopkeeper, do you have a private place where we can talk?"

"Of course, please follow me," the woman in red replied with a raised eyebrow, leading them upstairs to a private room.

Her shop wasn't large, but it had several private rooms specifically for serving important customers, especially those with substantial needs.

After closing the door, the woman in red gracefully took a seat, her lips curling slightly as she poured tea for them. "What does the honored guest need? Rest assured, no one can hear us here."

Shu You relaxed and exchanged a glance with Huanxi before saying, "I want something that can... arouse desire. Preferably something that would leave a man unable to move but still responsive."

Her expression remained calm, her gaze steady.

This was the result of her inquiries over the past two days. The first time, Shu You had been too embarrassed to ask with people coming and going, her face flushed red. She had only dared to speak up after everyone had left.

Now, looking at the alluring shopkeeper, Shu You was certain that she would find what she needed here.

"We have plenty of such items. What kind would the honored guest prefer?" The woman in red laughed upon hearing this, her beauty captivating.

Without hesitation, Shu You replied, "The most expensive, with the strongest effect."

She had plenty of money, and since she didn't have many opportunities to come down from the mountain, she wanted to buy everything she needed in one go to avoid having to return.

After a pause, she added, "I want enough for thirty uses."

The storybooks mentioned only twenty, but Shu You wasn't sure, so she decided to buy extra. If there was any left over, she could just discard it.

The woman in red's eyes sparkled with even greater amusement. Her lips, as red as peonies, parted slowly, her breath like orchids. "What form would the honored guest prefer? We have incense, pills, and liquid potions."

Shu You pondered for a moment, "The incense, then."

The woman in red slowly stood, bowed, and turned to leave, but Shu You called out to stop her. A blush crept onto her fair face, and she seemed a bit embarrassed.

"Actually, I'll take all of them. I want everything."

"Yes," the woman in red nodded with a smile, swaying her hips as she left. When she turned away, she couldn't hide the smile on her face. A big spender!

She returned with an array of bottles and jars, placing them on the round table and introducing each item's use to the two girls.

Shu You listened intently, her small face filled with surprise.

The woman in red picked up the only black porcelain bottle, her eyes filled with subtle pride. "This is our shop's specialty. Just one drop can cloud a man's mind, leaving him at your mercy."

As she spoke, she mimed grabbing something in the air to demonstrate.

Shu You instantly understood and nodded as if she had known all along. Looking at the assortment of items on the table, she felt more at ease. With so many options, at least one should work. She silently ranked them in her mind, planning to test them on Xiao Ling in a few days.

Shu You suddenly thought of something and asked the shopkeeper, "Do you have anything to prevent pregnancy? Something that doesn't harm the body and has a long-lasting effect?"

She certainly didn't want to get pregnant. It would be best if such a thing existed.

If she stayed away from home for a long time and returned with a child in her belly, her mother would be furious. Just thinking about her mother's angry face made Shu You shrink her shoulders involuntarily.

"Of course, we have such items, and they don't harm the body," the woman in red replied, even more delighted. She quickly turned and went out.

After paying, Shu You had the items labeled and packed into a wooden box, which Huanxi carried downstairs.

As they were about to leave, the shopkeeper slipped a silk-wrapped bundle into Shu You's hands and raised an eyebrow with a teasing smile. "Take your time, honored guest. This is a gift. I hope you find it enjoyable. Come again if you need anything."

The mysterious gift piqued Shu You's curiosity. She shook it and heard a faint metallic clinking inside.

She racked her brain but couldn't figure out what it was. With the bustling street, it wasn't convenient to open it there. After Huanxi took it from her, she soon forgot about it.

"Miss, shall we return today?" Huanxi asked, holding the wooden box and walking beside her. They had rented a carriage two days ago and could return to Changshan Temple at any time.

Shu You looked at the vendors lining the street and lost interest in strolling. Since she had already obtained what she most wanted, continuing to wander didn't seem appealing. She nodded, "Let's go back."

The two of them slowly made their way back to the inn, stopping occasionally along the way.

...

Xing Jue folded his hands over his abdomen, his gaze silently fixed on the lord seated before him. The round table was laden with pastries and delicacies, untouched, and the tea had grown cold after only a few sips.

For the past two days, His Highness seemed distracted. He had stopped chanting scriptures after a short while and returned to his room, doing nothing but copying scriptures, barely eating.

Xing Jue's sharp senses picked up on the unusual behavior and thought something major must have happened. Later, he discovered that Miss Jiang hadn't appeared for several days.

It dawned on him then, this was the root of the problem.

After some investigation, he learned that Miss Jiang and her maid had left the mountain early two days ago, their whereabouts unknown.

Fortunately, all the furnishings and items in her room were still there. Perhaps she was just taking a short break and would return in a couple of days.

He reported this news to His Highness, who only paused for a moment before responding with a noncommittal "Mmm," but Xing Jue could see the deep disappointment in his master's eyes.

He couldn't help but feel a pang of envy. He hadn't expected His Highness to be so affected by love.

Seeing that His Highness was losing his appetite, Xing Jue had an idea and softly suggested, "Your Highness, I've heard there are many street performance troupes in the city. Why not go and take a look?"

"Those places attract crowds. Who knows, you might even run into Miss Jiang."

Xiao Ling glanced at him with a faint look, his pen-holding hand unchanged, his tone calm. "Do you have nothing better to do?"

Xing Jue immediately fell silent, but now, as he looked at his master's back, he couldn't help but feel a sense of helplessness and the urge to complain.

Wasn't he supposed to be very busy?

How did he end up coming out here?

Tsk tsk, a man of contradictions.

Xing Jue's gaze followed the open window of the second-floor private room toward the main street, lost in thought.

Suddenly, a familiar figure appeared in his line of sight. His eyes widened in surprise, shining brighter and brighter. He couldn't help but lean forward and say, "Your Highness, I've seen Miss Jiang."

"I'll go and invite them up."

Xiao Ling, who had just lifted his teacup, paused and glanced out the window. His expression remained unreadable. "Then invite them up."

"Yes," Xing Jue quickly exited, taking large strides downstairs.

chapters.title: She Had No Use for That
chapters.content:
Shu You was standing in front of a street stall, listening to the owner's relentless sales pitch. She had no interest in the small trinkets, but the owner had a gift for gab, a real smooth talker.

"This hairpin is made of genuine ivory, polished smooth and shiny. Since it's your first time here, I'll let you have it for just five taels of silver."

Huanxi's eyes widened in shock. Five taels for an ordinary hairpin? Her monthly allowance was only five taels. This was daylight robbery!

She quickly freed her hand and tugged at Shu You's sleeve, signaling her not to fall for it.

Shu You gave her a reassuring look, then leaned slightly forward, feigning the innocence of a naive girl as she examined the other items on the stall. "Such a precious item for only five taels? The shopkeeper, you are too kind."

The owner beamed with delight, his small eyes squeezed into slits by the surrounding flesh. "That's right, that's right. Thank you for the compliment, miss. The most important thing in business is honesty."

Shu You let out a soft laugh and was about to speak again when a voice interrupted her.

"Miss Jiang, how have you been?"

"Xing Jue! What are you doing here?" Shu You turned her head and was surprised to see him. Her eyes widened with a hint of unexpectedness. "What a coincidence."

Xing Jue smiled slightly and gestured toward a nearby restaurant. "It is a coincidence. Our young master is also there. Why not come up and sit for a while, Miss Jiang?"

Shu You followed his gaze to the second floor of the restaurant, where Xiao Ling was indeed present.

Go up and sit with him to chat and reminisce? Shu You recalled the cold expression on his face the last time they met, and a flicker of fear passed through her heart. She shook her head. "Thank you for the invitation, but it's getting late, and we need to hurry back to Changshan Temple by carriage. Maybe next time."

After saying this, she gave an embarrassed smile, took Huanxi's hand, and left immediately. She couldn't afford to provoke him; she didn't want to see Xiao Ling's cold face.

Right now, Shu You only wanted to sleep with him, not to engage in idle chatter.

"Eh? Eh?" Xing Jue didn't have time to stop them and watched as they left. He couldn't help but sigh. Now this was a fine mess. He had spotted them, but they didn't want to see his master.

Then again, it made sense. His master only had that one good feature, his face. With such a terrible and stubborn temper, how could Miss Jiang possibly like him?

Xing Jue sighed again, resigned to his fate as he went back to report.

Footsteps echoed outside the door. Xiao Ling suddenly straightened his back, his thoughts in disarray. What should he say when he saw her?

He could say it was just a coincidence, that he hadn't come out specifically to look for her, and tell her not to read too much into it.

His gaze fell on the pastries and dishes on the table. He didn't know if she would like them. The tea had gone cold and would need to be replaced.

The door creaked open and then shut. Xiao Ling pretended to glance casually toward the entrance. When he saw that there was no one behind Xing Jue, his gaze faltered slightly. Where was she?

Xing Jue didn't dare to lift his head, his voice low. "Your Highness, Miss Jiang said she had something to do and didn't come up..."

The room remained silent for a long time. Xing Jue held his breath, not daring to make a sound. He regretted suggesting that they go out for a stroll.

"Miss Jiang said she's returning to Changshan Temple now. Maybe we could…"

"It's none of my concern what she does," Xiao Ling set down his teacup heavily, his thin lips pressed into a straight line. If she didn't want to come, then so be it. He didn't care.

"Return to the palace."

His clear voice carried a hint of suppressed anger. Xing Jue, fearing he might provoke him further, responded softly, "Yes."

He quickly followed the figure in front of him, sighing inwardly. His Highness was in such a foul mood; he wondered if he would be able to endure the poison flare-up in three days.

...

The sound of horse hooves came to a stop at the gate of Changshan Temple. Shu You led the way back to her small courtyard with Huanxi.

"Miss, who was that person just now?" Huanxi asked hesitantly, the words lingering on her lips the entire way, as if she wasn't sure whether she should ask.

Shu You didn't hide anything from her. She leaned on the table, resting quietly, her eyes tightly closed as if she might fall asleep at any moment. This trip had exhausted her.

"That was his servant."

She didn't mention the name, but Huanxi understood and nodded slowly. She was about to find a place to store the wooden box and the silk bundle.

Without opening her eyes, Shu You stretched out her hand toward her. "Give me that silk bundle. I want to open it and see what's inside."

"Yes," Huanxi replied, placing the bundle in her hand. She then turned and bent down to find a corner to put the wooden box.

Shu You mustered some energy and sat up straight. She had been wanting to open it for a long time but had restrained herself because they were always out in public.

Her fingers worked to untie the bundle, and a segment of silver chain appeared. She continued to unwrap it, and when she saw the full item, her mind went blank. A blush of shyness colored her watery eyes. It was a set of chains.

An intimate aid for lovers.

This was too extravagant; she had no use for it.

Shu You quickly covered it up and restored the bundle to its original state. Even after a long time, her heart was still pounding, and with each breath, she could feel her eardrums vibrating along with her chest, thump, thump, very clearly.

She quickly stood up and stuffed the bundle into a pile of clothes, out of sight. It took a long time for her to calm down.

"Miss, when will we... implement the plan?"

Huanxi's words interrupted her thoughts. Shu You suddenly came back to her senses. After a moment of hesitation, her resolve hardened. She steeled her heart. "In three days."

Whether it was early or late, death was inevitable. It was better to get it over with quickly.

The sun rose and then set, and the night grew so dark that one couldn't see their own hand in front of them.

After bathing, Shu You tucked several types of potions into her sleeve. She wasn't sure which one would work, so she decided to bring them all.

"Miss, I'll wait for you in the room," Huanxi said, a hint of worry appearing on her face as she stood guard at the door.

"Alright, I'll be back soon," Shu You replied with a calm expression, though her heart was filled with anxiety and tension. The hand hidden in her sleeve was shaking. "I'm going now."

She walked into the night, exuding a courage that embraced death.

Her graceful figure carried a lantern as she walked through the darkness. Shu You felt a pang of fear; she had never realized how dark the night could be. She was afraid that someone might suddenly jump out and scare her.

Fortunately, she walked at a decent pace, and Xiao Ling's small courtyard was just ahead.

Shu You stood at the entrance, hesitating for a moment before biting her lip and using a thin stick to pick the lock through the door crack. With a click, the door silently swung open before her.

This was a method she had thought of in advance. The courtyard walls were too high to climb over, so she had learned this trick. Fortunately, it worked.

She carefully closed the door behind her and headed straight for the main house. She didn't rush to open the door but instead crouched down, taking out the incense from her sleeve and blowing it forcefully through the crack in the door.

She blew until she was out of breath. When no more smoke came out of the small hole in the wooden barrel, Shu You silently crouched on the ground and waited.

It was supposed to take a quarter of an hour to take effect. She would wait.

She looked around nervously, her heart in her throat. Although the courtyard was quiet and deserted, if Xing Jue noticed, all her efforts would be in vain.

She didn't know how long she waited. Her feet had fallen asleep, and she carefully shifted her position, peering through the door crack into the room, feeling uncertain. It should have worked by now, right?

She used the same method to open the door and cautiously slipped inside, closing the door before standing up straight.

Shu You quietly surveyed the room. In the upper right corner, behind the bed curtains, she could vaguely make out a figure lying down.

She took one careful step at a time, lifting a corner of the curtain with her fingers. She saw the man lying on the bed, his face flushed and his eyes tightly closed. Shu You immediately relaxed and let out a breath of relief. It had worked.

chapters.title: Otherwise, Next Time Then
chapters.content:
The man’s exposed skin at the white collar of his robe was flushed deep red, his brows tightly furrowed, and fine beads of sweat dotted his forehead.

He looked as if he were in unbearable agony.

Shu You widened her eyes slightly in shock, stepping forward to try and touch his cheek with the back of her hand. The scorching heat under her fingers startled her.

So hot!

This incense was surprisingly potent!

She hadn’t even given him the medicine yet, just a small bamboo tube of incense had such a strong effect. The money was well spent.

The unconscious man’s lips moved as if he were trying to speak. Shu You jumped in surprise, leaning closer only to realize he was muttering deliriously.

“So hot… so thirsty.”

Shu You patted her chest in relief, he just wanted water. The sudden scare had nearly stopped her heart.

*Doing something guilty, afraid of ghosts knocking at the door.*

She turned and saw a cup of tea on the round table. Standing up, she poured a cup and returned to the bedside. But she hesitated, how could he drink while lying down? He might choke.

She placed the cup on the low stool beside the bed, then used all her strength to help him sit up against the edge of the bed. By the time she turned to grab the cup, his scorching body had already leaned against her. The man collapsed softly into her arms.

His breath was burning hot, spraying against her chin and tickling her.

Shu You turned her head slightly. Why was he so heavy? Dead weight! She pressed the cup to his lips, but he refused to open his mouth.

“Be good, aren’t you thirsty?” In the quiet night, Shu You’s voice was unmistakably clear as it entered the man’s ears. Finally, he parted his lips slightly, allowing the water to slowly pour in.

After finishing the cup, Shu You looked at Song Ling, who was leaning against her, and hesitated. Her hand rested on his cheek for a moment before she intended to pull away, but he pressed his face against her palm and rubbed it.

Her palm burned.

Should she take off his clothes first?

Shu You swallowed hard as she looked at the man’s loosened inner robe, her hands trembling with nervousness. She closed her eyes and pulled the thin belt from his waist, the knot loosening immediately.

Under the bright moonlight, the man’s chest and abdomen were shockingly pale. After two quick glances, she didn’t dare look again.

With shaking hands, she laid him back on the bed. Just as she was about to take a break, the man, unwilling to leave, pulled her into a tight embrace. A low, hoarse voice reached her ear, barely audible.

“So comfortable… don’t go.”

Shu You turned her face and buried it in his chest, so quiet she could hear her own heartbeat. Under her skin was his firm, scorching flesh, and the scent of sandalwood filled her nose.

It smelled so good.

She couldn’t resist taking a few deep breaths. Looking at his excessively handsome, delicate face, she thought to herself, *He’s the one who pounced on me, so it’s not my fault.*

With her eyes tightly closed, her lashes trembled slightly. She tilted her head toward his perfectly shaped thin lips, pressing against them for a moment before pulling back.

When he didn’t react, she pressed her lips against his again.

Shu You’s kiss was incredibly awkward. She was so nervous she didn’t know what to do. After a long time, she finally enclosed his thin lips and gently sucked, wetting his lower lip with a glossy sheen.

Soft, muffled sounds filled the small, curtained window.

His breath between her lips made her head spin, sending shivers through her entire body.

Shu You didn’t know what was wrong with her, she only felt that the man before her, Song Ling, was becoming more and more captivating. His brows, eyes, and straight nose were all to her liking. She wanted to devour him in one bite.

He smelled so good.

She pressed her lips against his again. Unexpectedly, he unconsciously parted his teeth, licking her lower lip, which startled her.

*He couldn’t be awake, could he?*

She stiffened her back and looked over, only to find his eyes still tightly closed. Reassured, she boldly entangled with him.

After who knows how long, she hooked her arms around his neck and turned her head to breathe. This was too torturous.

After just a short while, she was already covered in a thin layer of sweat. Softly leaning against Song Ling’s neck, she panted. At this point, she was having second thoughts. *Otherwise, next time then.*

Kissing was already this difficult, what about later?

This was unbearable.

As she hesitated and pulled back slightly, she didn’t notice the man in front of her had quietly opened his eyes. His pupils were deeply red, hazy and scattered.

“Mmm,” Shu You’s chin was lifted by a large hand. Her slightly parted lips were sealed shut. She widened her almond-shaped eyes in shock as the man’s scorching breath completely enveloped her.

His ragged breathing was urgent, and his hoarse voice lingered in her ear.

“So comfortable… I like it so much.”

Her entire body stiffened as she stared at the trembling lashes before her. All her awareness was concentrated on her lips. His scorching lips and teeth carried his unique breath, rolling and grinding in a sticky, lingering manner.

Shu You gradually found it hard to breathe and wanted to turn her head away for a moment to catch her breath.

The man sensed her attempt to retreat. A strong palm slid from her chin into the hair at the back of her head, tightly trapping her, forcing her to press even closer, unable to pull away even a little.

Shu You’s nose touched his. Every breath she took was filled with his scorching air. Her mind was so muddled she couldn’t think at all.

Her back sank into the soft mattress, their long hair entangling together.

…

After everything was over, Shu You struggled to sit up. The sky was already beginning to brighten. She had to return to the small courtyard before the monks’ morning chant, she couldn’t be seen.

Bearing her shame, she wiped away the traces on herself and Song Ling. After dressing him and restoring everything to its original state, Shu You stood up to leave.

She paused at the door for a few seconds, then turned back and opened the window a crack.

The room smelled a bit strange. If she didn’t air it out, someone might notice.

Shu You quickly left the small courtyard, retracing her steps back. Upon opening the door, she saw Huanxi dozing off at the entrance, her head slowly sliding down as she propped herself up with her arms.

“Huanxi,” Shu You opened her mouth to call her, but her own voice startled her. Why was it so hoarse? She couldn’t help but turn her head and cough a few times.

The sound woke Huanxi, who was half-asleep. She suddenly opened her eyes and saw her mistress’s current appearance, her eyes reddening. “Miss…”

Her lips were swollen, and there were several deep red marks on her fair neck. It looked alarming.

“I’m fine,” Shu You said with a smile to reassure her. She wasn’t lying. Although the process had been a bit painful, the unprecedented comfort she felt afterward was real.

She finally understood what the storybooks meant by “feeling light all over afterward.”

It was as if a long-standing illness in her body had been completely swept away. In two lifetimes, this was the first time she had felt like this, like a normal person.

Able to run, jump, with a steady heartbeat, a normal person.

Huanxi hummed in response, wiping away the tears from the corners of her eyes. She stood up and said, “I’ll go boil some hot water for you, Miss. It’ll be ready soon.”

“Okay,” Shu You supported her waist and sat down in the room. She was sticky all over and wanted to bathe as soon as possible.

As she sat in the bath tub, the hot steam made her face flush. Her thoughts drifted far away.

She had cleaned everything up. Song Ling had been drugged, he shouldn’t have any memory of it, right?

The shopkeeper had said that after inhaling that incense, one wouldn’t remember a thing. But Shu You was still a little panicked.

For the next few days, she would stay in the room and not go out. Anyway, her body was sore all over now. If she happened to meet him and it triggered a moment of memory, that would be bad.

Once her body recovered, she would go again. She had plenty of incense.

After making up her mind, Shu You got up from the bath tub, letting Huanxi dry her body and wring out her hair before lying down on the bed, drowsy.

The soft mattress beneath her involuntarily reminded her of what had happened earlier. Song Ling had been in so much discomfort, moaning but unable to find the right spot.

Shu You hugged the blanket and couldn’t help but let her mind wander. *He… must be a virgin, right?*

As she drifted off to sleep, she remembered she hadn’t recorded the count. Tomorrow, she would have to find a notebook to write it down. Otherwise, she wouldn’t even know how many times they had…

---

chapters.title: Miss Jiang is a Blessing!
chapters.content:
A raging fire burned through Xiao Ling’s body, scorching his meridians and blood, sweeping through him like flames across a grassland, leaving nothing unburned. Everywhere it passed brought intense pain, making his entire body tremble.

This pain was familiar. Every time the fire poison acted up, he had to endure it until it passed. When he woke up, he would be drenched as if he had waded through water.

But today was different. Amid the scorching heat, a trace of icy cold seeped in, like the chill of an ice and snow world, freezing the heat layer by layer. Xiao Ling shivered with comfort, involuntarily drawing closer to the source of that relief.

Soft, muffled sobs echoed in his ears all night long. The pleasure and comfort spreading through Xiao Ling’s body reached every limb, making his spine weak and his muscles tremble slightly.

In his hazy consciousness, he seemed to see Shu You. Her glistening, flushed eyes seemed to hold hooks that pulled him endlessly downward, bewitching him until his mind was unclear, sinking together with her.

The next moment, Xiao Ling opened his eyes, the corners red with unbearable heat. He stared at the canopy above, panting heavily, his chest rising and falling rapidly.

He seemed not yet fully awake from the dream, his expression dazed. He supported his forehead and slowly sat up.

Why did he dream of her again?

Or… was it such a dream? Xiao Ling recalled the scenes from the dream. His back instantly stiffened like a stubborn rock, not daring to relive it further. He quickly rolled out of bed.

It wasn’t until his toes touched the cold floor that he slowly realized what was happening. He stared blankly at his toes, lost in thought. Normally, after the poison acted up, he would have to lie in bed for a whole day before he could get up. How come today…

Outside the door, Xing Jue heard the movement inside and knocked lightly, calling out in a low voice, “Your Highness, are you awake? Physician Qin is waiting outside.”

It had become routine for the imperial physician to come after the poison acted up.

Xiao Ling suddenly came back to his senses, pulling himself out of his chaotic thoughts. His expression returned to its usual coldness. Sitting back on the bed, he said, “Come in.”

With a creak, Xing Jue entered with the white-haired Physician Qin. Seeing the prince extend his wrist for diagnosis, he glanced to the side, his gaze suddenly pausing as he noticed something was off.

This window had been closed last night, how did it suddenly open? Could it be that His Highness had opened it himself out of boredom yesterday?

But he wasn’t the type to do things himself. Xing Jue’s expression was hesitant, with a hint of confusion.

Physician Qin placed his fingers on the inside of Xiao Ling’s wrist, feeling his pulse for a moment. His brows furrowed before a hint of joy appeared in his eyes. He looked up at the man sitting upright on the bed, then felt his pulse for a long time before finally standing up.

“Your Highness is fine. Just take the medicine as usual.”

Xiao Ling, sitting on the bed, showed no reaction in his eyes. His thick lashes were half-lowered, as if he were lost in his own thoughts and couldn’t pull away.

The two outside had long grown accustomed to his coldness. Xing Jue, with a faint smile on his lips, saw the physician out. Since the physician said there was nothing serious, it meant yesterday’s poison attack wasn’t severe, good news.

Physician Qin bowed and picked up his medical case. Just as he was about to leave, with one foot already out the door, he turned back and said, “However, Your Highness must take care of your body. Do not indulge excessively, restraint is necessary.”

With that, he walked out. The two who left didn’t notice the man on the bed, whose pupils trembled at these words.

Xiao Ling’s eyes lost focus. He looked down and pulled open his collar, revealing a few light red marks on his abdomen. His scattered gaze fixed on them in a daze.

His fingers, gripping the thin rope of his inner robe, turned white. So it wasn’t a dream…

Xing Jue followed behind Physician Qin, confused. What did “do not indulge excessively, restraint is necessary” mean? His Highness hadn’t gone anywhere yesterday.

Before the physician left, Xing Jue decided to ask for clarification. He looked back at the open door of the main room and asked in a low voice, “Physician Qin, what did you mean just now? I don’t understand.”

Physician Qin frowned and looked him over. “You are the closest person to His Highness. You don’t know?”

His gaze seemed to say that Xing Jue was useless, just eating without doing anything, knowing nothing.

Xing Jue let out a dry laugh, his voice suddenly rising before he quickly covered his mouth. “His Highness’s thoughts are twisted in seven or eight ways. How could I know everything?”

Physician Qin saw that he genuinely didn’t know, so he explained, “Today, I could tell at a glance that His Highness’s body is much better. It must be due to the harmony of yin and yang with a woman of pure yin. You didn’t know about this?”

Now Xing Jue was truly stunned. His eyes widened as the image of Miss Jiang flashed through his mind. Could it be…

Could they have really done it?

Physician Qin saw his expression and chuckled before leaving leisurely. “Figure it out yourself.”

This old stubborn man. Xing Jue shook his head with a smile, his mood brightening as he closed the door. He walked slowly back to the main room and stood by the bed. “Your Highness, the hot water is ready.”

After waiting for a long time without a response, Xing Jue looked up to see him staring blankly at one spot, lost in thought. He called out softly again, “Your Highness?”

Xiao Ling finally came back to his senses and hummed in response. Without even putting on his shoes, he stood up and walked toward the side room bathroom.

“Your Highness, your shoes,” Xing Jue reminded from behind. Only then did he react and turn back to put them on.

Xing Jue sensed something was wrong but didn’t dare ask. From behind the screen, he asked, “Do you need this servant to assist you?”

“Get out,” came the cold voice, slightly hoarse.

Xing Jue pursed his lips. It seemed he wasn’t needed. He quietly retreated.

In the misty white steam of the bath, Xiao Ling submerged himself in the water, the surface not covering his head. His thoughts became clear at this moment.

The physician’s words just now were like a wildfire, awakening him. Those waves of pleasure weren’t an illusion or a dream, they had really happened.

Miss Jiang had truly been with him last night…

At this thought, the muscles in Xiao Ling’s chest and abdomen under the water suddenly tensed, hard as a rock.

They had truly been entangled, skin to skin. Xiao Ling suddenly surfaced from the water, gasping for air, his breathing heavy like a swimmer about to drown.

The warm water enveloped his entire body, and the residual heat on his skin was washed away in the water. It felt like tender palms slowly caressing him. An indescribable emotion surged in his heart, and his breathing became unstable.

How dare she…

Xiao Ling knew she admired him, but he never expected Jiang You to be so bold.

They weren’t even married, yet she had sneaked into his room at night and… And then, in the morning, she left without a trace. If it weren’t for the fragments of memory he still retained, would she have pretended nothing happened?

What did she take him for?

Xiao Ling’s gaze darkened with an unclear emotion. The frustration in his chest had no outlet. His hand under the water clenched tightly, veins bulging. The man was cold and stern, terrifying.

Warm light streamed in through the window, shining on the clear water and creating ripples. The light fell on his fair, jade-like profile, reflecting on the water’s surface. His slightly downturned lips made him look inexplicably like a large dog abandoned by its owner, longing for its master’s pity.

After who knows how long, the man, who had been as still as a stagnant pool, finally moved. His gaze gradually cleared and became determined as he looked at the corner where the girl had appeared last time, deep in thought.

Xing Jue waited silently outside. When he heard the door open behind him, he immediately turned around.

The refined man’s hair was still dripping with water droplets. Without stopping, he walked past, leaving only one sentence: “You don’t need to be present these next few nights.”

Xing Jue responded blankly, “Yes.”

Not needing to be present meant leaving space for His Highness and Miss Jiang. Xing Jue realized this and his breath hitched, he was overjoyed.

It seemed His Highness had finally figured it out. Miss Jiang was actually the woman of pure yin. What a stroke of luck, it had come without any effort.

Miss Jiang was truly a blessing.

chapters.title: Why Keep Staring at Her?
chapters.content:
The morning breeze was gentle, and the golden sun rose slowly, carrying the dampness of dawn.

Shu You had taken two days to recover from her soreness. She didn’t even know what Song Lengsheng was made of, so big, yet every movement had once pulled with a sharp, aching sting.

Fortunately, Huanxi had brought some medicinal ointment, which soothed the pain considerably.

She wasn’t in a hurry. She’d wait a few more days before going again. Visiting too frequently wouldn’t be good.

Just thinking about that day made Shu You’s face burn. Anyway, her body was in perfect condition now, it would definitely last her a long time.

As she stood up, apart from the lingering soreness, Shu You felt an unparalleled comfort, as if she were floating on air, unaware of where she was. She lifted the wooden basin filled with clothes with ease, as if she could even go and perform a chest-breaking stone act.

"Miss," Shu You heard Huanxi’s voice approaching from afar. She smiled, quickened her pace, and ran up to her, her tone slightly unsteady. "The main hall is quite lively. Would Miss like to go take a look?"

Shu You picked up a handkerchief and wiped the fine beads of sweat from Huanxi’s forehead. Her voice was so soft it was almost unreal. "What’s the rush? Changshan Temple’s grand Dharma assemblies happen every month."

"But..." her tone slowed, a mischievous glint flashing in her eyes. "Since Huanxi has invited me, I simply must take a look."

Huanxi’s already flushed cheeks turned even redder. Excited, she nodded, and followed Shu You as she stood up and walked toward the main hall.

In the past, at the Marquis’s residence, she had rarely gone out. Now that she was free from restraints, she wanted to see as much as she could. Once she returned to the residence, it would be hard to be this free again.

The two of them stood by the side railing, looking at the open space in front of the main hall, which was now packed with people.

Normally, the first and fifteenth days of the month were crowded, but she hadn’t expected it to be this packed today.

"Miss, let’s not go down. We can just watch from here."

Shu You hummed in agreement. She had originally wanted to join the crowd, offer some incense, and donate some money, but the sea of people had completely discouraged her.

The noisy crowd suddenly fell silent. Several monks in robes slowly emerged from the main hall. The one leading them had white-streaked hair and kind, gentle features.

She followed their gaze and heard the whispers from the people below the stone railing. The word "Chen" reached her ears.

Was this Abbot Chenle?

Shu You had heard of him before, and today, she finally saw him in person.

"Let’s come to offer incense tomorrow or the day after, when there aren’t as many people," Shu You decided, turning to Huanxi and whispering. As her gaze wandered, she noticed a pair of eyes fixed on her.

Shu You followed the gaze and saw Song Ling standing by a stone pillar not far away. The shadow of the pillar obscured half of his refined figure.

His exquisite face alternated between light and shadow, and his deep, dark eyes were as cold and indifferent as ever, as if the madness they had shared on the bed that day had been nothing but her delusion.

She abruptly averted her gaze. What was he staring at her for?

Caught off guard by the sudden encounter, Shu You, as if she had done something guilty, quietly shrank behind Huanxi, blocking most of the prying eyes. Only then did she feel a little better.

After a while, she couldn’t resist and stole another glance.

Song Ling’s gaze was still fixed on her.

Shu You suddenly straightened her back, as if sitting on pins and needles. Watching Huanxi’s enthusiastic expression beside her, she bit her lower lip, enduring for a few moments before she couldn’t take it anymore and spoke, "Huanxi, I’m not interested in this Dharma assembly. I’ll go back first."

"Then I’ll go with Miss…"

"No need. I can go back by myself. I know the way," Shu You waved her hand reassuringly. It was rare for Huanxi to have a chance to go out, and she didn’t want to ruin her fun. After saying goodbye, she silently left via the stairs beside her.

If she couldn’t provoke him, she could at least avoid him. She would go back to her room and not go anywhere. Let’s see how Song Ling would keep staring at her then.

Shu You lowered her head and quickly walked through the corridor. Suddenly, a man appeared in front of her. Fortunately, she dodged in time and avoided a collision.

The man had flushed cheeks, reeked of alcohol, and let out a few hiccups as he spoke, filling Shu You’s nose with the stench.

"Pretty little thing, where are you going? Want big brother to keep you company?"

Shu You frowned immediately, covered her mouth and nose, and took a few steps back. She didn’t intend to engage, but the man blocked her path as she tried to pass by.

"Hey, don’t leave," the drunken man stretched out his arm, blocking her way, and tried to grab her sleeve.

"What are you doing!" Shu You nimbly dodged, glaring at him. Who was this man? How dare he be so rude!

How could there be such a person in the sacred grounds of Changshan Temple?

"Don’t walk away," the drunk man slurred, blocking her path again, still trying to grab her sleeve.

"Get lost!" Shu You’s body was agile as she dodged again, glaring at him. This man was unbearably rude!

Changshan Temple was a Buddhist sanctuary, how could there be such a person here?

"Feisty little beauty, I like that. How about you come with big brother for some fine food and drink down the mountain?" The man’s under-eyes were dark, looking like he had overindulged in lust and was drenched in the stench of alcohol and greed. He slowly approached Shu You.

As he looked at the beautiful young girl before him, a wicked fire burned in his heart. He wished he could take her back to his mansion as his twenty-third concubine.

"Pretty little thing, don’t be afraid. Big brother will be good to you."

Shu You stood there, seemingly frozen in fear, but in reality, she was contemplating where to kick him.

Daring to provoke her, did he have a death wish? She glanced at the man’s lower body, her right foot itching to move.

Her eyes flickered with impatience as she waited for the right moment. In an instant, she decided, now!

Before her right foot could lift, the man in front of her disappeared like a gust of sharp wind. Instinctively, she closed her eyes. A moment later, she heard a loud splash. The man who had been in front of her was now flailing in the pond beside the corridor.

"Save me! I am…" The man’s mouth filled with water as he splashed around, unable to speak clearly.

Shu You was stunned. A figure silently landed beside her. A familiar, gentle voice spoke, "Miss Jiang, are you alright?"

She came to her senses and saw Xing Jue standing beside her at some point. As her gaze shifted between him and the man in the water, she realized it was Xing Jue who had saved her. Still in shock, she said, "Thank you."

Thanks to him, she didn’t have to deal with that scoundrel any longer.

"You don’t need to thank me," Xing Jue smiled and waved his hand, stepping aside to reveal the figure not far behind him. "It was my master’s order."

Shu You followed his gaze and her pupils suddenly widened. She couldn’t help but swallow hard.

Why had he followed her?

She couldn’t move forward or backward.

Xing Jue smiled and bowed beside her, then lightly tapped the water’s surface a few times before taking the drunken man away, disappearing without a trace.

Song Ling stood in her inevitable path, his cold, beautiful dark eyes locking firmly onto her.

As if he had waited for a long time and she still hadn’t come over, Song Ling began to walk toward her, step by step.

The sound of his shoes touching the tiles seemed to amplify endlessly, just like Shu You’s rapid heartbeat, thumping loudly.

He was now close, standing right in front of her. Shu You’s lips curved into a stiff smile, and she lowered her gaze, not daring to look at him. "Master Song."

Song Ling looked at the fluffy top of her head. The usually bold and reckless girl didn’t even dare to lift her head. He suddenly found it amusing.

Wasn’t she the one who liked him so much? Now she couldn’t even speak.

A soft "mm" came from above her head. Shu You’s hand under her sleeve pinched her palm hard to keep calm, not allowing herself to show fear.

He didn’t know what she had done yet. There was no need to be afraid.

She looked up and met his gaze, those deep, ink-like eyes. Feigning composure, she said, "Thank you just now."

"No need to thank me. It was nothing," Song Ling’s expression didn’t change. He glanced at the calm water, and a flicker of fierceness and killing intent flashed deep in his pupils.

That fool had a death wish.

Shu You waited for a few moments but didn’t see any sign of him leaving. She forced a laugh, "I won’t disturb you any longer."

Why was he still standing there motionless!

She lowered her head and tried to walk past him, but his figure blocked her path completely.

What did this mean? Shu You’s eyes showed confusion as she looked up at him.

Only then did Song Ling step aside and stand shoulder to shoulder with her. His tone was open and incredibly natural. "I’ll walk you back."

"No, no need," Shu You almost cried out. Realizing her overreaction, she softened her voice, "No need to trouble Master Song. I can…"

chapters.title: A Deadly Silence
chapters.content:
This man’s attitude had completely changed after just two days without seeing her.

Had he been possessed by a ghost?

Or did he find out?

Shu You’s heart was confused, and a sudden thud echoed within her. As their eyes met, she collided with his dark, sunken gaze. His lips were tightly pressed, and his expression was no different from usual, except for the slight lack of impatience.

Judging by his appearance, he probably didn’t know. She had checked carefully before leaving, and there had been no problems.

Reassured, she was certain he didn’t know. If he did, he might have already come to strangle her.

Otherwise, how could he have been kind enough to drive away that scoundrel for her just now?

Lost in thought, Song Ling had already walked several steps ahead. He stood to the side, silently watching her. Shu You quickly caught up, and the entire way was unbearably awkward. She didn’t speak, and neither did Song Ling, he was like a mute.

The two of them walked side by side in silence toward her courtyard. The sandalwood scent from his body continuously wafted into Shu You’s nose with the wind, and she couldn’t help but take a few deep breaths.

Her small courtyard was now in sight. Shu You was overjoyed, finally, they had arrived.

"Master Song, I’m here. Thank you," Shu You pressed her lips together, restraining the joy in her heart. Finally, they had arrived. She couldn’t wait to send this "Buddha" away.

But the man merely gave a faint "mm" and didn’t leave. His clean, clear voice softly reached her ears. "Don’t you have anything else to say to me?"

Say what? Shu You’s hand under her sleeve paused slightly, and her body stiffened. The forced smile on her face almost slipped.

"No, I don’t. Does Master Song have something to say to me?"

As soon as the words left her mouth, she admired her own psychological resilience. Just a moment ago, her mind had heated up, and she had almost blurted out an apology. Fortunately, she had held back.

Shu You forced a laugh. "I’ve arrived. Ha ha, let’s talk another time."

With that, she fled like a rabbit, disappearing from sight.

The man left standing in place lowered his gaze and suddenly let out a soft laugh. He stared in the direction she had left for a long time before finally walking away.

A rabbit that refused to confess the truth deserved to be punished.

Shu You had been hiding behind the door the whole time, not daring to move. Only when the footsteps had faded into the distance did she dare to breathe a sigh of relief. She keenly sensed that Song Ling’s repeated appearances were unusual.

It was as if he knew something and had come to demand an explanation.

But he hadn’t reacted strongly either, leaving Shu You uncertain and unwilling to confirm. She could only guess.

Her heart was uneasy, and for a moment, she was afraid of seeing him again. She decided to wait a few more days before going to his courtyard. The longer she could delay, the better.

The plan was wonderful, but reality was cruel.

The next day, as evening approached, Shu You’s entire body began to itch. It wasn’t a superficial itch on her skin but rather an itch that seemed to seep out from her meridians.

She had never felt this way before and didn’t know what was wrong with her.

"Miss, should I go call a doctor?" Huanxi stood beside her, seeing her reddened eyes from the unbearable sensation. Worry appeared on her face. Miss had applied the ointment, but it had no effect at all.

Shu You’s expression was normal, and her body temperature wasn’t high. She didn’t have a fever, but her entire body felt as if it were being roasted by fire, with an indescribable heat and tingling sensation rising within her. Only when her cheek touched the cool, round table did she feel a slight relief.

Why did it feel like she had been poisoned? But she hadn’t taken anything.

The thought flashed through her mind, and Shu You suddenly stood up, as if realizing something. She walked straight to the bed, lifted the pillow, and pulled out the book to flip through it.

Her fingers quickly turned the pages, and finally, on the back cover of the blue binding, she noticed some faint traces. However, the handwriting was dark and unclear against the royal blue cover.

Shu You quickly took the book to the candlelight to examine it closely, then let out an explosion.

"Ahhhhhhh, damn it!"

The courtyard echoed with her shout. Huanxi hurried over, urgently asking, "What’s wrong? What happened?"

Shu You was on the verge of tears, her voice filled with helplessness. "It’s nothing. I know what’s wrong with me now."

She suspected that the author of this book had deliberately tricked her, hiding the most important thing under the book cover. She had flipped through this book several times and had never noticed it.

After the "medicine guide," apart from her monthly cycle, she had to have intercourse every three days, or she would experience the symptoms she was feeling now, utterly unbearable.

Shu You supported her forehead and sighed, enduring the wave of weakness in her chest. Even after drinking several cups of tea, her throat was still parched.

Moreover, only intercourse would work. Other forms of intimacy would only alleviate the symptoms.

Silence. A deadly silence.

She looked at the book with the blue cover, unable to speak. Not long after, another wave of overwhelming emotions hit her. Shu You bit her lower lip to keep from moaning.

Shu You’s gaze passed through the window, looking in the direction of Song Ling’s courtyard. An idea suddenly formed in her mind.

Go! Go tonight!

Night fell, and the cicadas chirped ceaselessly.

After bathing, Shu You endured the itching and quickly walked along the bamboo path. After a short quarter of an hour, she saw the tightly closed courtyard gate and sighed in relief.

She took out her "tools" and was about to squeeze through the gap in the door when, in the next moment, she pushed lightly, and the door actually opened.

Shu You: ?

Today was surprisingly smooth.

She was too uncomfortable to think much about it. After closing the door, she went straight to the main house and blew in the sleeping powder.

After waiting for a long time, she cautiously entered the room, moving as quietly as a cat.

With a soft creak, the sound of the door opening was especially clear in the quiet night. She was extremely careful, afraid of waking Xing Jue and ruining everything.

Only after closing the door did she breathe a sigh of relief. She slowly walked to the bed, lifted the mosquito net, and sat down.

Song Ling was lying on the bed, his eyes tightly closed, as if he were in a deep sleep.

Shu You boldly lifted his quilt and reached out to untie the knots of his inner robe. As her hand accidentally touched his warm, smooth abdominal muscles, she couldn’t help but sigh in admiration. His skin was really nice.

She couldn’t resist touching him again. It was so firm. She poked his abs with her fingertips, but it didn’t feel particularly good.

She clicked her tongue a couple of times. With a body like this, what was the point? But then she thought, it was convenient for her.

Otherwise, if he had a big belly, she wouldn’t have the appetite.

She lowered her head and continued to struggle with the thin rope of his trousers. Her small face was filled with concentration. Why was it so hard to untie today?

"Do you need help?"

A familiar voice came from above her head, making her freeze on the spot. Her almond-shaped eyes widened suddenly. Had she heard wrong?

It must be an illusion. It had to be.

The man’s voice continued, shattering her fantasy.

"Why aren’t you speaking?"

She still didn’t react. Song Ling’s patience had worn thin. He pinched her chin, forcing her to look up. "Have you gone mute?"

He had deliberately waited for two days, and finally, she had come to him. He wanted to ask her what she meant by this.

Sleeping with him and then running away, avoiding him, was that supposed to be fun?

His expression was clear to Shu You. There was not a trace of tenderness in his eyes.

Today, for some reason, the sleeping powder had no effect on him.

But it had worked perfectly last time. Could the shopkeeper have tricked her with fake goods?

Even in the face of death, Shu You’s mind was filled with wild thoughts. She looked at those cold eyes, which were as indifferent as ever, and a hint of fear rose in her heart.

She was probably going to meet her end today.

Fear overpowered the heat in her body. Countless ideas flashed through her mind. She resorted to her old trick, wrapping her arms around the man’s waist and burying her face in his chest. Warm breath fanned his fair chest.

"Woo, I didn’t want to, but I just like you too much."

"Like you so much that I can’t help myself, which is why I’ve resorted to this."

chapters.title: Love You So Much I Can't Escape
chapters.content:
Again.

Xiao Ling was already on guard, and this tactic no longer worked on him. He stretched out a finger and gently pressed it against her forehead, pushing her away. "Speak properly."

Propping himself up on his elbow, he casually closed his robe. Sitting up, his tall figure towered over Shu You by a large margin. In the narrow bed curtains, with just the two of them, his large frame exuded an oppressive and dominant presence.

He had already made up his mind to question her clearly when he ordered Xing Jue not to appear these past few days, setting a trap to catch her like a turtle in a jar.

Tonight, lying in bed, he had no sleep at all. His mind was filled with thoughts of what to do once he caught her. The mere thought of her panicked and trembling expression made the corners of his mouth twitch slightly.

Reckless and willful mistakes deserved punishment. Otherwise, if she could drug him today, who knew what crazy things she might do tomorrow.

The girl before him had a sea of grievance in her eyes, but Xiao Ling's heart was as hard as a rock. He knew she did this for him, that her crazy infatuation, unrequited, had driven her to take such risks. But this was not the right path, and he needed to properly correct her nature.

Shu You let out an "ouch," wrinkling her eyes as she was pushed away. Seeing him staring at her intently, she knew everything she had done was exposed.

No wonder he had asked her if she had something to say last time. No wonder the courtyard gate wasn't locked today and opened with just a push. So he had been waiting for her to come.

This guy was so scheming. Shu You pouted, her mind racing. Kneeling on the bed, her legs twitched, ready to escape.

Running away was shameful, but effective.

"A live dog is better than a dead lion." She glanced at the door, calculating how long it would take to get there from where she was.

Xiao Ling saw through her little trick. The girl's eyes darted around, clearly up to no good.

She wouldn't be able to leave now. He reached out and tightly grabbed her wrist. Her skin was soft and tender, boneless. He unconsciously loosened his grip slightly, but not enough for her to break free.

"Why aren't you speaking? Usually, your mouth is quite sharp." Xiao Ling found it amusing. He tugged at her wrist, pulling her closer, so close he could smell the light, sweet fragrance on her.

Shu You, caught off guard, almost crashed into his chest. The numbness and heat on her body quickly spread throughout her entire being under the tension. The itch in her bones made her want to moan softly, but she bit her lip to stop herself.

She tried to pull her hand away, but he held it even tighter. Shu You's face burned as if it were on fire, and her mind felt feverish. Dazedly, she stared at the plump, round lips right under her nose, a strong desire rising in her heart.

If he wouldn't let her leave, then she wouldn't leave.

She tilted her head slightly, propping herself up, and crashed into him. Their lips met, and she kissed and nibbled at his thin lips, recklessly drawing in the breath between his lips and teeth.

Xiao Ling was stunned for a moment. When he reacted and tried to turn his head away, the girl had already tightly wrapped her arms around his neck, inseparable.

This was outright audacity!

Originally, the large hand holding her wrist let go and pushed at her waist, but the girl was faster. Her knee pressed against his leg, her hand locked behind his head, pinching his chin as she deepened the kiss. A grown man was left with no way to deal with her.

Shu You kept sucking on his lips. Over time, she was no longer satisfied with this shallow contact. But he seemed to be stubbornly resisting, keeping his teeth tightly closed, refusing to respond.

She mischievously reached out and pinched the sensitive area at his waist where his robe was open. At the same time, she bit his lower lip. The man in front of her suddenly trembled in pain, letting out a hiss. She seized the opportunity and finally tangled her tongue with his.

But kissing couldn't completely relieve the craving in her body. The thin air in her chest made her lean against the man's shoulder to catch her breath. Her soft, continuous moans made the nearby ear turn red as blood.

"You are absolutely..." Xiao Ling felt both anxious and angry. Taking advantage of her momentary rest, he pushed her away and leaned against the bed frame, panting.

She had actually kissed him forcefully without any regard. Did she really think he couldn't do anything about her?

He was just about to scold her again when he saw her watery, misty eyes and stopped. His heart was filled with a bit more irritation. Why was she crying again?

He hadn't even said anything harsh yet.

Xiao Ling pressed his lips together, letting her shrink into his embrace with tearful eyes. His palm rested on the bed beside his legs, his exquisite profile exuding a hint of stubbornness under the hazy moonlight.

Hot tears flowed down her fair chest and abdomen, as if scorching his heart. The bedsheets beneath him were suddenly gripped tightly, wrinkling.

"I can't live without you," Shu You, through his open robe, hugged his slender waist tightly. Her cheek pressed against his chest, and she cried so hard she could barely breathe. There was no lie in her sincere and natural expression; she really felt like she was about to die.

Xiao Ling's entire body stiffened upon hearing this. The muscles in his back tensed, and he frowned. "What nonsense are you talking about?"

Did she really admire him that much? To the point of spouting nonsense.

Seeing that he didn't believe her, Shu You suddenly tightened her arms around him. She couldn't help but sob a few times. "Everything I said is true. I can't live without you. Let me stay, okay?"

Her warm fingertips traced his waist, sending shivers through Xiao Ling's body, making him tremble involuntarily.

Shu You thought he was trying to push her away again. No matter what, she wouldn't let go. She directly straddled his legs, burying her entire body into his shoulder, and softly coaxed, "Okay?"

The small window curtains were silent. Neither of them spoke.

Shu You only rubbed her forehead against the side of his neck to relieve the heat in her body. The faint sandalwood scent helped a little.

The man in front of her lowered his eyelashes, slightly trembling, lost in thought. She didn't urge him, knowing that if he didn't refuse, it was as good as agreement. Occasionally, she planted light kisses on his neck.

Xiao Ling was indeed struggling internally. He hadn't expected the girl to be so deeply in love with him, to the point of swearing her devotion with her life.

The sincerity in her words, that she wouldn't see the sun of the next day if he pushed her away, made his heart ache. No one had ever said such words to him, insisting that it had to be him.

But her status was low. Bringing her into the Eastern Palace would cause some trouble. Once he set a precedent, the petitions from those officials would surely flood in.

Moreover, he had never been with a woman before. Suddenly having a member of the opposite sex by his side would make him uncomfortable.

As Xiao Ling was lost in thought, soft lips moved from his jaw to the corner of his mouth. In the entanglement, he tasted the salty tears from her mouth, mixed with the sweet fragrance on her body. It was like a sweet and sour plum fruit. After the first taste, he couldn't stop.

He sighed silently, looking at the girl before him who had her eyes tightly closed, depending on him as her only support. Gradually, he began to yield.

Fine. Even though her low status was troublesome, it wasn't impossible to handle. At worst, he could find a family to elevate her status. Even if he suddenly brought her into the palace, no one would be able to say anything.

Dealing with those old foxes in the court wasn't something that could be done in a day or two. He had plenty of ways to handle them.

Xiao Ling felt that he didn't have much affection for her, but they had already been intimate like a married couple. Since she liked him so much and couldn't live without him, keeping her around wouldn't be difficult.

His palm caressed the girl's waist. Looking at her pitiful, reddened eyes, his hoarse voice carried a hint of seriousness. "Do you really admire me? Is it me and no one else?"

Shu You heard a glimmer of hope. She climbed further up, cupping the man's face firmly. "Of course. I love you so much I can't escape. If you don't want me, I can only die."

---
